findings.title: The dimension that decides the winner is stamped missing_data and reported 'N/A' in the same payload — a 4% price gap produces a 14-point 'clear lead' attributed to nothing
findings.evidence: Ran compute_scores on two electronics products with IDENTICAL specs, both 4.5 stars / 900 reviews / identical fact_check, prices 50 vs 52 BHD (PROD flags). Result: overall [72.0, 58.0], win_margin 14.0. breakdown p0 = {'performance_score': 50, 'value_score': 100.0, 'build_quality_score': 50, 'feature_score': 90.0, 'ecosystem_score': 50, 'futureproof_score': 90.0}; missing_data = ['performance_score','value_score','build_quality_score','ecosystem_score']; dimension_winners = {'value_score': 'N/A', ...}. value_score is the ONLY dim that differs (100.0 vs 30.0) and supplies 0.20*70 = 14.0 = the entire margin. Cause: _signal_missing_for (scoring_service.py:328-334) defines the value dim's missingness as 'spec OR price missing', while _compute_value_score (:1200-1207) RETURNS the real price score when spec is gone — so the cell is simultaneously numerically real, decisive, and flagged absent. Reproduced in 9/9 categories on the 5-vs-5000-BHD pair: margin 7.0-14.0, dimension_winners[value dim]='N/A', missing0=True in every one.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p2.py (section 'EXTREME PRICE RATIO') and p4.py (section 'build_scores_summary text vs the decisive dim'). Minimal: from app.services.scoring_service import get_scoring_service; A={'name':'A','brand':'B','category':'other','specs':{...full...},'price':{'amount':5,'currency':'BHD','source_method':'local_bhd'},'rating':4.0,'review_count':300}; B=same specs, amount 5000; get_scoring_service().compute_scores([A,B]) -> win_margin 10.5, breakdown value_score 100.0/30.0, missing_data contains 'value_score', dimension_winners['value_score']['winner']=='N/A'.
findings.impact: Every consumer that reads missingness rather than the number contradicts the winner. compute_dimension_winners (:2465) returns N/A, so build_scores_summary (:2829) — the text fed to the GPT verdict prompt — literally prints 'value: stronger' and 'Dimension leaders: ... value=N/A, core function=N/A, ...' plus 'Score winner: Brand A (clear lead)' in the same block. The verdict model is asked to justify a clear lead while being told every dimension leader is N/A or tie; that is a direct driver of fabricated justification (compounds M18 PO-prompts-01/02). The user-facing dimension table shows no-data on the one row that decided the ranking. Hits the single most common real comparison shape: two similar products a few percent apart in price.
findings.fix: Split 'the signal behind this dim is absent' from 'this dim contributed nothing'. In _normalize_scores, stamp `_{dim}_missing` for a value-type dim only when BOTH spec and price are missing (i.e. when _compute_value_score actually returns the MISSING_SCORE sentinel) instead of the current spec-OR-price rule at :2231/:328-334; when only one side of the blend is gone, keep the dim measured and record the degraded provenance in a new additive key (e.g. `partial_dims`) so the FE can caption it 'price only'. Independently, make the winner explainable: if the argmax margin is carried by dims that compute_dimension_winners calls N/A, build_scores_summary must not print 'clear lead' — emit 'too close to separate on measured dimensions'. Ship behind a new dark flag ENABLE_VALUE_DIM_PARTIAL_SIGNAL (default OFF) so the flag-off goldens stay byte-identical.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_value_dim_missing_contract.py::test_decisive_dim_is_never_reported_missing — build the 50-vs-52-BHD identical-spec electronics pair, call compute_scores, compute the per-dim contribution to (overall[0]-overall[1]), and assert that no dim contributing more than 1.0 point of the margin appears in either product's missing_data or resolves to 'N/A' in dimension_winners. Red at HEAD (value_score contributes 14.0/14.0 and is both).
findings.dedupe: new — M18 PO-rubric-07 covers the undampened _normalize_price cliff that MAKES the 4% gap worth 70 dim points, and PO-rubric-03/#101 covers the MISSING_SCORE injection; neither reports that the deciding cell is simultaneously stamped missing and rendered N/A. still-open

findings.title: The B0-A array tie-collapse turns EQUAL MEASURED signal into claimed missing data: two fully-specified, equally-rated, equally-fact-checked products get 4 of 6 dimensions stamped no-data
findings.evidence: scoring_service.py:2113-2155 collapses reliability_scores, popularity_scores and spec_scores to MISSING_SCORE and sets `_<sig>_missing=True` on BOTH products whenever `len(set(scores))==1 and scores[0] != MISSING_SCORE`. Measured (PROD flags): two products with the SAME full spec dict, both rating 4.5, both review_count 900, both fact_check {verified 8, likely 2, price_verified True} -> electronics missing_data=['performance_score','value_score','build_quality_score','ecosystem_score'] (4/6), makeup 4/6, other 4/6, and every one of those dims resolves to dimension_winners 'N/A'. Two products with PERFECT, fully-verified fact_check (reliability_raw 1.0 -> 100.0 each) are reported as having no reliability data and their dim value is dragged from 100.0 to the 50 sentinel. Census over the whole PROD grid: 464/864 product_0 dim cells (53.7%) carry a missing_data stamp.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p4.py (last two sections). Minimal: A and B identical full-spec electronics, both rating 4.5, review_count 900, fact_check {'specs_verified':8,'specs_likely':2,'specs_flagged':0,'specs_unverified':0,'price_verified':True,'review_sentiment_consistent':True}, prices 50 and 52 -> compute_scores(...)['scores']['product_0']['missing_data'] == ['performance_score','value_score','build_quality_score','ecosystem_score'] and breakdown performance/build_quality/ecosystem == 50 (not the measured 100.0/98.0).
findings.impact: The comparison the product exists to serve — two genuinely similar, well-documented products — is the one it reports the least data for. Every equally-strong signal is deleted, so the ranking is decided only by whatever happens to differ (here a 4% price gap, see PO-RUBRIC-01), the overall scores are pulled toward 50, the missing-dimension coverage KPI (count_missing_dim_cells, :3742) is inflated by design rather than by extraction failure, and the FE/verdict see 'no data' for facts the pipeline actually paid to fetch. The B0-D justification quoted in the comment ('ZERO genuine non-MISSING ties observed across the corpus') was measured on a 24-query 2026-06 sample and does not hold for same-product/same-brand pairs.
findings.fix: Stop conflating 'tied' with 'absent'. Keep the collapse ONLY where it was diagnosed — a tie whose underlying raw signal is itself a sparse-coverage artifact — by gating each of the three blocks on evidence of sparsity (e.g. reliability: total fact_check buckets < 3 on both sides; popularity: review_count is None on both sides; spec: scored_fields/total_fields below CATEGORY_MIN_COVERAGE on both sides). A genuine tie must keep its real value and take the existing _DIM_NORM_TIE path (65 dampened) rather than the 50 sentinel, and must NOT set `_<sig>_missing`. Ship behind ENABLE_TIE_IS_NOT_MISSING (default OFF) and regenerate the four *_flag_off_golden.json only for the flag-ON arm.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_tie_collapse.py::test_equal_strong_signal_is_not_reported_missing — two products with identical full specs, identical 4.5 ratings, identical 900 review counts and identical fully-verified fact_check; assert missing_data is None/[] for both and that breakdown['build_quality_score'] reflects the measured reliability (>=90), not 50. Red at HEAD (4/6 dims stamped, all three at 50).
findings.dedupe: new — the collapse blocks are documented in-code as the B0-A v2.1/v2.2 phantom-tie fix and are not in the M18 PO-rubric set; M18 PO-rubric-03/#101 is about the 50 sentinel's ARITHMETIC, this is about the sentinel being INJECTED over real data. still-open

findings.title: fashion and `other` (the fallback category) have no numeric spec fields at all, so _score_specs returns exactly 1.0 for every product above min coverage and the spec + value dims are erased from every such comparison
findings.evidence: HIGHER_IS_BETTER_BY_CATEGORY['fashion'] = set() and ['other'] = set(); LOWER_IS_BETTER_BY_CATEGORY['fashion'] = set() and ['other'] = set() (scoring_service.py:262-286). _score_specs (:1789-1826) therefore takes the `total_score += 1` presence branch for EVERY populated field, so total_score/scored_fields == 1.0 exactly for any product at or above CATEGORY_MIN_COVERAGE (0.30 for both). Measured through _compute_raw_scores on two DIFFERENT full fashion products (leather/handmade/Italy vs canvas/machine/CN): spec_raw A=1.0, B=1.0; same for `other` (steel/Germany/2yr vs plastic/CN/1yr) -> 1.0 / 1.0. The tie then trips the :2145 spec collapse, so missing_data = ['craft_score','cpw_score'] (fashion) and ['function_score','value_score'] (other) on a pair where BOTH sides are fully specified. The 5-units-vs-5000-units pair scores win_margin 0.0 for fashion and other while the same gap scores 14.1-18.6 in the seven categories that do have numeric fields.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p2.py (section 'SPEC-DIM COLLAPSE with BOTH products fully specified'). Minimal: svc._compute_raw_scores({'category':'fashion','specs':{material:'leather',style:'tote',...10 fields}}, 'fashion')['spec_raw'] == 1.0 and the same for any other fully-populated fashion product; compute_scores on the pair -> missing_data ['craft_score','cpw_score'].
findings.impact: For fashion, craft_score (weight 0.25) + cpw_score (0.10) = 35% of the score is deleted; for `other` — the destination of every category the classifier cannot place, i.e. the largest real bucket — function_score (0.25) + value_score (0.15) = 40% is deleted, and value is exactly where price would have entered. The residual ranking runs on review count, star rating and LLM fact-check only. The spec dimension for these two categories can never distinguish products on merit; the only thing that can move it is how many schema fields the extractor happened to fill (see PO-RUBRIC-13), so 'Craftsmanship' and 'Core function' are measuring extraction coverage, not the product.
findings.fix: Two parts. (a) Make the presence branch informative for these categories: change _score_specs' neutral credit from a constant 1.0 to a per-field discriminator (populated-and-non-generic = 1.0, populated-but-boilerplate = 0.5, absent = 0), or route these categories through the #100 pair-relative path unconditionally — ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM's _apply_spec_field_normalization (:1872) already scores one-sided fields 1.0 vs 0.0 and would restore discrimination on coverage differences even with no numerics. (b) Independently of (a), never let a 1.0-vs-1.0 tie be laundered into `_spec_missing` (the PO-RUBRIC-02 fix). Do not add numeric HIGHER_IS_BETTER entries for fashion/other without a unit table — that reintroduces PO-rubric-01.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_fashion_other_spec_dim.py::test_spec_dim_can_separate_two_fashion_products — two fashion products with clearly different craftsmanship/material/origin and identical field COUNT; assert breakdown['craft_score'] differs by more than the 3.0 dimension-winner tie margin and that 'craft_score' is not in either missing_data. Red at HEAD (both 50, both stamped missing).
findings.dedupe: new — M18 PO-rubric-01 is the opposite failure (raw magnitude summing where numerics DO exist); the two categories with NO numerics were not covered. still-open

findings.title: Nominal weights do not control the score: unequal per-signal dynamic ranges make the LLM fact-check dim the top effective driver in 8 of 9 categories while the price-bearing value dim is the weakest at ~7%
findings.evidence: The six signals reach the breakdown through different normalizers with different ranges: _normalize_dimension (:2297-2367) dampens spec/spec_secondary into 45-85 (span 40); _normalize_review (:2369) maps into 20-100 (span 80); _normalize_direct (:2378-2383) maps reliability and popularity straight into 0-100 (span 100, no dampening, no tie tolerance); _normalize_price (:2274) into 30-100 (span 70). Effective influence = weight x span, computed for all 54 dims: electronics build_quality_score (w 0.15, reliability) = 23.4% of total effective influence vs performance_score (w 0.25, spec) = 15.6%; supplements safety_score (w 0.25, reliability) 36.6% vs efficacy_score (w 0.30, spec) 17.6%; the nominal top-weighted dim is NOT the effective top driver in 8/9 categories (only makeup ties). The value dim — the only carrier of price — is the LOWEST effective driver in 7/9 (6.9%-11.0%). Confirmed live: on one mixed electronics pair, dimension_winners margins were build_quality_score 94.0 vs performance_score 7.2 with the same product ahead on every spec field.
findings.repro: python -c "import app.services.scoring_service as S; RANGE={'spec':40,'spec_secondary':56,'review':80,'reliability':100,'popularity':100,'value':49,'price':70}; [print(c, sorted(((d, round(100*S.CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS[c][d]*RANGE[S.ScoringService._DIMENSION_SIGNAL_MAP[c][d]]/sum(S.CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS[c][x]*RANGE[S.ScoringService._DIMENSION_SIGNAL_MAP[c][x]] for x in S.CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS[c]),1)) for d in S.CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS[c]), key=lambda t:-t[1])) for c in S.CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS]" — full table in scratchpad/porubric (p2/effective-range run).
findings.impact: The weight table is the product's stated policy (it is also serialized to clients as weights_used and category_weights) and it does not describe what actually happens. The signal with the widest swing is the one the pipeline trusts least — reliability comes from the LLM fact_check bucket counts, which M18 PO-fact-check-01/03/07 already showed can be satisfied by absence of evidence — so a fact-check artifact outranks a measured spec lead. Every offline weight sweep, every 'we raised performance to 0.25' product decision, and the personalization caps (which are expressed as ratios of these weights) are computed in units that do not reach the score.
findings.fix: Normalize the ranges before applying the weights so weight is the only lever: put every signal through the same dampened band by routing reliability and popularity through _magnitude_aware_ratio into _DIM_NORM_FLOOR_DAMPENED/_SPAN_DAMPENED (45-85) exactly as spec already is, and give review and price the same treatment (price is already M18 PO-rubric-07's open item — do them in one change). Then re-ratify CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS against the corrected engine, because today's weights were tuned against the distorted ranges. Ship behind ENABLE_UNIFORM_DIM_BANDS (default OFF); the flag-off goldens stay byte-identical and the flag-on arm needs its own golden.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_effective_weight.py::test_effective_influence_matches_nominal_weight — for each of the 9 categories, drive each dim from its worst to its best attainable breakdown value while holding the others fixed, record the resulting delta in `overall`, and assert the ordering of those deltas matches the ordering of CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS. Red at HEAD in 8/9 categories.
findings.dedupe: new — extends known:M18/PO-rubric-07 (still-open), which reports the undampened 70-point cliff in _normalize_price only; the 0-100 undampened band in _normalize_direct and the resulting nominal-vs-effective weight inversion are not in that finding. Compounds known:M18/PO-rubric-06 (labels misdescribe what is measured) by showing the mislabelled dims are also the strongest.

findings.title: At exact score parity the winner is whichever product the caller passed first — the coverage tie-break exists but is gated behind a dark flag, so prod has no tie-break at all
findings.evidence: scoring_service.py:1486 `winner_index = overalls.index(max(overalls))`. The only tie-break (:1490-1505, prefer the product with fewer missing_data entries) is guarded by `if renorm_enabled and len(overalls)==2 and overalls[0]==overalls[1]` — ENABLE_MISSING_DIM_RENORM is absent from the Railway `web` var list, so at prod flags there is NO tie-break. Measured over the 1008-run grid in both product orders: overall SCORE SETS are perfectly order-symmetric (0/1008 asymmetric), but 119/1008 runs return the same winner_index in both orders — i.e. the winner follows input position, not the product. At PROD flags 13/144 (9.0%) of runs are exact ties and ALL 13 are order-dependent: 9x `identical` (one per category), plus fashion and `other` on both the notation-gap and the 1000x-magnitude pairs (where the two products genuinely differ in a spec field, see PO-RUBRIC-03, yet score identically).
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/gen.py then an.py — sections 'ORDER-DEPENDENT rows' and 'ASYMMETRIC overalls'. Minimal: build any fashion pair differing only in a numeric spec field; compute_scores([A,B])['winner_index']==0 and compute_scores([B,A])['winner_index']==0.
findings.impact: The engine's contract is 'same input = same output (deterministic)' (module docstring, :1-6). It is deterministic but not order-invariant: the same two products swapped in the query string ('X vs Y' against 'Y vs X') crown different winners on ~9% of my grid, and the whole downstream stack (winner card, winner_evidence, tradeoff pairs, the verdict prompt's 'Score winner') follows. Worse, win_margin is 0.0 on those runs, so build_scores_summary still calls it a 'narrow lead' and the verdict is asked to justify a coin flip.
findings.fix: Move the tie-break out from behind the flag and make it order-symmetric and total: on `overalls[0]==overalls[1]`, prefer (1) more measured dims (fewer missing_data — the existing :1495-1505 logic), then (2) better price provenance (_price_authority_delta closer to 0), then (3) a deterministic content hash of brand+name so the result is stable under swap rather than stable under position. Independently, when win_margin == 0.0, suppress the winner claim: set a `too_close_to_call` flag the response builder and build_scores_summary honor instead of printing 'narrow lead'. The tie-break itself is behavior-preserving for every non-tied pair, so it can ship without a flag; gate only the `too_close_to_call` surface.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_order_invariance.py::test_winner_is_the_same_product_in_both_orders — parametrize over the 9 categories with an `identical` pair and a fashion notation-gap pair; assert compute_scores([A,B])['winner_index'] == 1 - compute_scores([B,A])['winner_index'] whenever the two overalls are equal, i.e. that the SAME product wins. Red at HEAD for 13/144 PROD cells.
findings.dedupe: new — the in-code comment at :1490-1497 acknowledges the degeneracy but explicitly scopes the fix to flag-ON ('Flag OFF is untouched (byte-identity)'); no M18/M13 finding and no open issue covers the prod-flag state. still-open

findings.title: The `other`-category price sub-scale is dead code: _normalize_scores never passes comparison_prices, so a 400 BHD item is tiered 'luxury' instead of 'budget' and the cross-tier value penalty fires on the wrong expectation
findings.evidence: scoring_service.py:2088 `price_tiers.append(self._detect_price_tier(price, category))` — the `comparison_prices` keyword is never passed (the only mention on the line above is the comment 'A.5.5 will wire comparison_prices for the other geometric-mean sub-scale', :2082). `_detect_other_subscale` (:515) has ZERO call sites outside the guarded branch at :546, and grep over app/ finds no other caller. So 3 of the 4 _OTHER_SUBSCALE_TIERS entries (other_mid/other_high/other_ultra, :507-513) are unreachable in production. Measured: _detect_price_tier(400.0,'other') == 'luxury' with no comparison_prices vs 'budget' with comparison_prices=[5000,6000]; _detect_price_tier(6000.0,'other') == 'top_tier' vs 'mid'.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p4.py (section '_detect_price_tier: is the other geometric sub-scale ever reached'). Also `grep -rn '_detect_other_subscale' app/` returns only its own definition and the one guarded call inside _detect_price_tier.
findings.impact: `other` is the fallback for every category the classifier cannot place, so this is the widest bucket. On the other_light scale everything above 189 BHD is luxury and everything above 500 is top_tier, so a laptop, a mattress or a car compared as `other` is always in the top two tiers. That feeds TIER_EXPECTATIONS (:580-590, luxury 0.88 / top_tier 0.90) into the cross-tier branch of _compute_value_score (:1213-1217, `value = 50 + (spec_score - expected*100)*0.8`): with spec_score capped at 85 by the dampened band, expected 88-90 forces the value dim to 50 + (85-90)*0.8 = 46 or lower for BOTH products, i.e. the value dim is pinned near/below the sentinel for every expensive `other` comparison. The Bundle C section 3f design is written, tested at the helper level, and inert.
findings.fix: Wire it: in _normalize_scores compute the price list once before the tier loop and pass it through — `prices=[rs.get('price_raw') for rs in raw_scores if rs.get('price_raw')]` then `self._detect_price_tier(price, category, comparison_prices=prices)`. _detect_price_tier already no-ops the sub-scale for the 8 named categories and for `other` when fewer than 2 prices are present, so the change is scoped to `other` pairs with two real prices. Ship behind ENABLE_OTHER_SUBSCALE (default OFF) because it moves price_tiers, price_tiers_by_index, is_cross_tier and therefore the value dim for a whole category — then measure the cross-tier rate before flipping.
findings.test_first: tests/test_price_tier_other_subscale.py::test_two_high_priced_other_products_are_not_both_luxury — compute_scores on two `other` products at 5000 and 6000 BHD; assert result['price_tiers_by_index'] resolves via the other_ultra scale (both 'budget'/'mid', is_cross_tier False) rather than both 'top_tier'. Red at HEAD.

findings.title: The documented +/-30% explicit-preference cap is exceeded by up to 43.65% in all 9 categories — 45% worse than the +32% M18 recorded
findings.evidence: _compute_weights (:1608-1618) clamps each dim to cat_default*(1 +/- MAX_WEIGHT_SHIFT_RATIO) and then renormalizes ONCE (`weights = {k: v/total ...}`) with no re-check — unlike _apply_capped_adjustments (:2673-2706), which the behavioral, cohort and session layers use and which iterates clamp-renormalize up to 3 times. Measured over all 8 priorities x 5 budgets x 9 categories (360 weight vectors): max realized |shift| = 0.4365 (haircare multi_value_score, priorities=['price'], budget='budget'), 0.3913 (makeup perf_value_score and skincare results_value_score), 0.3860 (supplements), 0.3833 (grocery, fragrances), 0.3778 (fashion), 0.3694 (other), 0.3665 (electronics). Every category exceeds 0.30. By contrast the other three layers hold: behavioral 0.1000-0.1004 (cap 0.10), cohort 0.1001-0.1008, session 0.0501-0.0506 (cap 0.05).
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p2.py (section 'PERSONALIZATION: realized shift vs the claimed +/-30% cap').
findings.impact: The cap is the stated guarantee that personalization nudges rather than rewrites the rubric; it is off by up to 45% of its own value. The overshoot lands on the value-type dim in 8 of 9 categories — the dim that carries price — so the layer that is supposed to be bounded is unbounded exactly where a price-first user's preference could flip a winner. M18 recorded the drift at +32%; the true worst case is 43.65%, so the recorded severity understates it.
findings.fix: One line of reuse: replace the clamp-then-renormalize block at :1608-1618 with a call to the existing `ScoringService._apply_capped_adjustments(weights, deltas, base_weights, MAX_WEIGHT_SHIFT_RATIO)` so the explicit path gets the same iterate-and-recheck loop as the other three layers (this is exactly M18 PO-rubric-12's prescription). No flag needed — it strictly tightens an existing documented bound — but regenerate any golden that pins a personalized weight vector.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_weight_caps.py::test_explicit_preference_cap_holds_after_renormalization — parametrize over all 9 categories x 8 priorities x 5 budgets, and assert abs(w[d] - CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS[cat][d]) <= CATEGORY_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS[cat][d] * MAX_WEIGHT_SHIFT_RATIO + 1e-9 for every dim. Red at HEAD in 9/9 categories, worst haircare 0.4365.
findings.dedupe: known:M18/PO-rubric-12 — still-open, with a corrected magnitude (0.4365 realized, not the recorded +32%) and the observation that it lands on the value dim in 8/9 categories.

findings.title: The runner-up card still fabricates a win from a data void — reproduced with a 44.0-point 'build quality' lead that is the MISSING_SCORE sentinel
findings.evidence: _loser_strongest_dim (:2616-2648) scans `loser_breakdown.items()` for the highest value with no reference to the loser's missing_data list, so the 50 sentinel competes with real scores. Reproduced at PROD flags on an electronics pair where the loser has NO fact_check at all and loses every real dim: loser breakdown = {'performance_score': 46.7, 'value_score': 17.0, 'build_quality_score': 50, 'feature_score': 36.0, 'ecosystem_score': 10.0, 'futureproof_score': 20.0}, missing_data = ['build_quality_score'], and compute_tradeoff_pairs returns loser_wins = {'dimension': 'build_quality_score', 'product': 'Brand B', 'margin': 44.0} — a 44-point advantage manufactured entirely from the absence of data (the winner's real reliability score is 6.0).
findings.repro: python -c with the pair in scratchpad/porubric (winner: full specs, price 40, rating 4.9, rc 2000, FC_BAD; loser: degraded specs ram 1 GB/storage 8 GB/battery 900 mAh, price 900, rating 1.0, rc 2, NO fact_check key) then svc.compute_tradeoff_pairs(r['dimension_winners'], ['Brand A','Brand B'], r['winner_index'], r['scores']).
findings.impact: The 'where the runner-up wins' card is the product's honesty surface for the losing option, and it can assert the loser's single best quality is a dimension the system has no data for — with a large, confident margin. Note also that the whole card is silently empty if a caller passes product_names that differ from the f'{brand} {name}'.strip() strings compute_dimension_winners was built with (the winner/loser name match at :2571-2578 is by string equality); the two production call sites (structured_comparison_service.py:3603 and :4322) do pass the matching list, so that is latent, not live.
findings.fix: In _loser_strongest_dim, skip any dim present in the loser's missing_data (available from scores[loser_key]['missing_data']) and any dim absent from the winner's breakdown, and return None when only such dims remain, so compute_tradeoff_pairs falls through to [] and the card stays empty rather than citing a void — exactly M18 PO-rubric-09's prescription, still unimplemented. Behavior-preserving for pairs with real loser strengths; no flag needed, but pin the empty-card case in a test so nobody 'fixes' the blank card by reintroducing the sentinel.
findings.test_first: tests/test_tradeoff_pairs.py::test_loser_strongest_dim_never_names_a_missing_dim — the reproduction pair above; assert every returned loser_wins['dimension'] is absent from scores[f'product_{1-winner_index}']['missing_data'], and that the result is [] when the loser's only 'best' dim is a sentinel. Red at HEAD (build_quality_score, margin 44.0).
findings.dedupe: known:M18/PO-rubric-09 — still-open at HEAD, now reproduced with a concrete fabricated margin (44.0) rather than a static reading.

findings.title: #101 status: no-data still beats measured-bad data at prod flags in 9/9 categories, and the ENABLE_MISSING_DIM_RENORM fix leaves the inversion intact in 4/9 via its own degenerate fallback
findings.evidence: PROD flags, `unrated_vs_2star` (two products identical in specs, price, review_count and fact_check; A has NO rating, B has 2.0 stars): A WINS in all 9 categories by 2.5-4.0 points (electronics 55.0 vs 52.0; makeup/haircare/fragrances 52.5 vs 48.5; grocery/other 53.8 vs 50.2), and A's missing_data lists ALL SIX dims while B's lists four — a product with zero surviving measured dimensions outscores one with two. Cause: _normalize_review (:2369) maps 2.0 stars to 40.0 while MISSING_SCORE (:297) injects 50. With ENABLE_MISSING_DIM_RENORM ON the flip is fixed for that pair but the `nodata_vs_measured_bad` shape (A has no price, no specs, no rating, no fact_check) STILL has the void winning in grocery/supplements/makeup/skincare (46.0 vs 42.6/44.7/44.5/45.8) because every dim is one-sided, `effective_weight_total` hits 0, the :1394-1405 degenerate guard logs and falls back to the un-renormalized legacy sum. At PROD the same shape has the void winning in 6/9 (50.0 vs 42.6-47.5). win_margin==0.0 census: PROD 13/144 (9.0%), ENABLE_MISSING_DIM_RENORM 31/144 (21.5% — 18 of the new zeros are exactly the rating-gap pairs 4.9-stars/900-reviews-vs-unrated and unrated-vs-2-stars, which become exact ties in all 9 categories), ALL_ON 45/144 (31.3%).
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/gen.py; an.py — sections 'NO-DATA OUTSCORES MEASURED' and 'WIN_MARGIN 0.0 rows'. Per-category tables in scratchpad/porubric/report.txt.
findings.impact: This is the live prod behavior, not a dark-flag one: a product the pipeline failed to gather data for beats a product it measured and found mediocre, in every category. The proposed fix does not close it for the worst shape (total data void) and buys a new problem — 21.5% of runs return win_margin 0.0, so 'clear lead' becomes structurally unavailable for the very rating gaps the app should be most confident about. That is the open product call on #101.
findings.fix: Two changes, both inside the existing flag. (a) Remove the sentinel's advantage rather than the dim: clamp the missing injection to the dampened band FLOOR (45) instead of the midpoint 50 so a data void can never outrank a measured 2.0-star (40.0) — this is the 'at minimum' half of M18 PO-rubric-03 and is independent of the renorm. (b) Fix the degenerate path: when `effective_weight_total <= 0` because ONE product is a total void, do not fall back to the legacy sum — return the orchestrator's INSUFFICIENT_DATA route for that side, or award the comparison to the measured product outright. (c) For the win_margin-0.0 residual, surface a `too_close_to_call` / `decided_on_coverage` reason alongside win_margin so the verdict text can say 'we could only separate these on data availability' instead of reporting a 0.0 margin with a confident winner.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_missing_beats_measured.py::test_no_data_never_outscores_measured_data — parametrize over all 9 categories x {unrated_vs_2star, nodata_vs_measured_bad} x {flag off, ENABLE_MISSING_DIM_RENORM on}; assert the product with strictly more measured dims has the strictly higher overall. Red at HEAD in 9/9 (flag off) and 4/9 (flag on).
findings.dedupe: known:#101 / M18 PO-rubric-03 — still-open, and the recorded fix is INCOMPLETE: fresh evidence that the flag-ON degenerate fallback re-opens the inversion in 4/9 categories, plus the quantified win_margin-0.0 residual (9.0% -> 21.5% -> 31.3%) that #101's open product question asks for.

findings.title: #100 status: unit notation still decides the winner by 18.7 points at prod flags (5000 mAh vs 5 Ah), and the fix flag converts that into an exact tie whose winner then reverts to input order
findings.evidence: PROD flags, two electronics products identical in every field except battery notation — '5000 mAh' vs '5 Ah' (the SAME capacity): overall [73.9, 55.2], win_margin 18.7, winner = the mAh product. _score_specs (:1802-1826) sums raw magnitudes so 5000 vs 5 dominates the mean. Same shape in the other 8 categories via their own higher-is-better field ('5 units' vs '5000 units'): margins 14.1-18.6 in the seven categories that have numeric fields, 0.0 in fashion and `other` (which have none — PO-RUBRIC-03). Conversely a GENUINE 32x storage gap (16 GB vs 512 GB, everything else equal) yields win_margin 0.3 because battery's 5000 swamps the sum. With ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM ON the notation case correctly collapses to 0.0 (the _SPEC_FIELD_UNIT_MISMATCH_RATIO=10 guard at :1930-1935 fires) — but 0.0 is an exact tie, and there is no tie-break at that flag combination, so winner_index falls back to input order (27/144 zero-margin rows under that flag, up from 13).
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/gen.py; an.py — section 'NOTATION / UNIT GAP pairs'. Golden suite re-run at HEAD: tests/test_scoring_spec_field_normalization.py passes (fixture spec_field_norm_flag_off_golden.json still matches).
findings.impact: Prod ships the pre-fix behavior: the electronics winner is decided by how the retailer wrote the battery spec, at 18.7 points, while a real 32x storage advantage moves 0.3. Flipping ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM removes the artifact but exposes PO-RUBRIC-05 — the notation pair becomes a tie decided by which product the user named first — so the two must ship together.
findings.fix: Flip ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM only after PO-RUBRIC-05's order-symmetric tie-break lands, otherwise every unit-mismatch pair silently becomes an input-order coin flip. Sequence: (1) land the unconditional tie-break + too_close_to_call, (2) re-run the four flag_off goldens, (3) enable ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM on Railway `web` (it is currently absent from the var list, i.e. default OFF), (4) re-measure the notation grid and confirm 0 non-zero margins on notation pairs and a non-zero margin restored on the 16-vs-512 GB pair.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_spec_field_normalization.py::test_notation_gap_ties_and_real_gap_separates — assert compute_scores on ('5000 mAh' vs '5 Ah', otherwise identical) yields win_margin 0.0 AND the same winner in both product orders, while ('16 GB' vs '512 GB', otherwise identical) yields win_margin > 3.0 for the 512 GB side. The second half is red under both flag states at HEAD (0.3 flag off, 0.0 flag on).
findings.dedupe: known:#100 / M18 PO-rubric-01 — still-open at prod flags; fresh evidence is the measured 18.7-vs-0.3 inversion (notation beats a real 32x gap 62x over) and the newly-measured flag-ON composition failure with the missing tie-break.

findings.title: #102 status: value_badge is asserted from the MISSING_SCORE sentinel — 'fair_price' is emitted for a product with no price and no specs — and the flag's honest-absence branch is unreachable
findings.evidence: apply_value_badges (:2496-2533) reads `value_score = breakdown.get(value_dim)` and skips only `if value_score is None` (:2522-2524). But _normalize_scores always writes a numeric for all six dims (:2225-2233), so breakdown.get(value_dim) is never None and the honest-absence `continue` is DEAD CODE. Measured: two `other` products with NO price and NO specs -> breakdown['value_score'] == 50 (the sentinel), missing_data lists all six dims, and both products get value_badge 'fair_price' — under BOTH flag states. Grid distribution over 2016 product-badge computations: PROD = 242 fair_price / 37 great_value / 9 premium_price / 0 overpriced (84% constant); ENABLE_CATEGORY_VALUE_BADGE ON = 87 / 147 / 53 / 1, i.e. the flag does move the badge off the constant as designed. Separately, response_builder.py:1703 emits `pd.get('value_badge', 'fair_price')`, so even if the skip branch were reachable the payload would default to the same claim.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p4.py (section 'value_badge from the MISSING sentinel') and p2.py (section 'VALUE BADGE distribution'). Golden re-run at HEAD: tests/test_value_badge_category_dims.py passes, value_badge_flag_off_golden.json still matches.
findings.impact: The badge is a price claim shown next to the product. Today it says 'fair price' about products the system has no price for, and it says it 84% of the time regardless of the data. Turning ENABLE_CATEGORY_VALUE_BADGE on fixes the constant-badge half of #102 but NOT the sentinel half — the badge is still asserted from a 50 that means 'no data', and response_builder's default would re-assert it even if apply_value_badges stayed silent.
findings.fix: Gate on missingness, not on None: in apply_value_badges skip when the value dim appears in that product's `missing_data` (or, once PO-RUBRIC-01 lands, when the dim's price leg is absent), and change response_builder.py:1703 from `pd.get('value_badge', 'fair_price')` to `pd.get('value_badge')` so an absent badge stays absent through the payload. Both belong inside ENABLE_CATEGORY_VALUE_BADGE so the flag-off golden stays byte-identical. Also note the 'overpriced' band (value_score < 25, :2542-2545) is unreachable on the same-tier path — the minimum attainable same-tier value score is 40.5 (spec floor 45 x 0.7 + price floor 30 x 0.3) — so it only ever fires cross-tier; either widen the band or delete it.
findings.test_first: tests/test_value_badge_category_dims.py::test_no_badge_when_the_value_dim_is_missing — two products with no price and no specs; assert 'value_badge' not in product (flag ON) and that response_builder's product payload carries rating-style None rather than 'fair_price'. Red at HEAD (both get 'fair_price' under both flags).
findings.dedupe: known:#102 / M18 PO-rubric-04 — still-open; the constant-badge half is fixed behind the flag (measured: distribution moves), the sentinel-as-claim half and the response_builder default are fresh and survive the flag.

findings.title: #103 status: at prod flags scoring_method lies in three directions — an inert preference set reports 'personalized', a dead behavior profile reports 'behavioral', and session dwell alone reports 'behavioral'
findings.evidence: Measured on an electronics pair, ENABLE_BEHAVIORAL_DIM_TRANSLATION OFF (the prod state — the var is absent from the Railway `web` list): preferences={'priorities':['nonexistent_priority'],'budget':'mid'} -> scoring_method 'personalized' with weights_moved=False; behavior_profile with legacy spec_score/review_score/price_score keys -> 'behavioral' with weights_moved=False (the keys intersect the electronics dim set nowhere); session_signals only -> 'behavioral' (no behavior profile exists). With the flag ON all three correct themselves: 'category_weighted', 'behavioral' (weights_moved=True), 'behavioral' (weights actually moved). The label branch is scoring_service.py:1524-1542; the legacy fall-through at :1533-1541 keys on input PRESENCE, not effect.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p2.py (section 'scoring_method LABEL matrix'). Golden re-run at HEAD: tests/test_behavior_dimension_translation.py passes, behavioral_flag_off_golden.json still matches.
findings.impact: `scoring_method` is a documented client contract and the field analytics uses to attribute personalization lift. Today it reports personalization that provably did not happen, so any measured 'personalized comparisons' rate is inflated, and the +/-10% behavioral layer that the label advertises is dead for 8 of 9 categories (it only intersects `other`'s review_score). Note the fix is written and tested — it just is not enabled on `web`.
findings.fix: This is a deploy decision, not new code: the label-by-effect branch and the legacy-key translation both live behind ENABLE_BEHAVIORAL_DIM_TRANSLATION and both behave correctly when it is on (measured above, and the 128-test golden suite passes at HEAD). Before flipping it, reconcile with #65 (behavior profile reads phantom columns, so dimension_sensitivity may be empty in prod anyway) — turning the translation on while the profile source is dead just moves the label from a false 'behavioral' to a true 'category_weighted', which is the correct outcome and should be verified against a real profile row first.
findings.test_first: tests/test_behavior_dimension_translation.py::test_scoring_method_reflects_effect_at_prod_flags — with the flag OFF, assert compute_scores(products, preferences={'priorities':['nonexistent'],'budget':'mid'})['scoring_method'] != 'personalized' and that a legacy-keyed behavior_profile that moves no weight does not yield 'behavioral'. Red at HEAD with the flag off (the current pinned behavior).
findings.dedupe: known:#103 / M18 PO-rubric-05 — still-open at prod flags, fix verified working behind the flag; fresh evidence adds the third case (session_signals alone mislabelled 'behavioral' under BOTH flag states, since :1533 and :1528 both treat session as behavioral).

findings.title: CATEGORY_MIN_COVERAGE re-verified NOT inverted, but it is a step function: one extra populated field multiplies the spec score by up to 1.43x at the threshold
findings.evidence: Recomputed the penalty for every k=1..n across all 9 categories (_score_specs :1821-1826, `penalty_factor = 0.5 + coverage_ratio` applied only when coverage_ratio < min_coverage). No category has min_coverage > 0.5, so penalty_factor is strictly < 1.0 below the threshold and exactly 1.0 at or above it — there is NO bonus row anywhere and no inversion. This CONFIRMS the M18 closeout. What the arithmetic does show is a discontinuity at the threshold: fashion and fragrances jump 0.7 -> 1.0 between k=2 and k=3 of 10 fields (a 30-point step, i.e. spec_raw multiplied by 1.4286); makeup and grocery 0.773 -> 1.0 (22.7 points); skincare/haircare 0.8 -> 1.0; `other` 0.786 -> 1.0 across k=2->3 of 7; supplements 13.6; electronics only 4.5.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p3.py (section 'CATEGORY_MIN_COVERAGE penalty arithmetic'); full k-by-k tables in scratchpad/porubric/p3.txt.
findings.impact: Low on its own, but it interacts with PO-RUBRIC-03: for fashion and `other` the presence-credit makes spec_raw a constant 1.0, so this step is the ONLY thing that can ever move their spec dimension — meaning the 'Craftsmanship' / 'Core function' dim in those categories is a pure function of how many schema fields the extractor filled, and a single extra field crossing k=3 opens a 30% relative gap that _magnitude_aware_ratio (tolerance 0.08) reads as decisive.
findings.fix: Make the discount continuous so extraction luck cannot cliff-edge the score: replace the branch with an unconditional smooth multiplier, e.g. `min(1.0, 0.5 + coverage_ratio / min_coverage * 0.5)` or simply divide by total_fields rather than scored_fields (the ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM path at :1943-1947 already uses `mean * (0.5 + scored_fields/total_fields)`, which is continuous — adopting the same shape on the legacy path removes the step). Ship inside ENABLE_SPEC_FIELD_NORM rather than as a separate flag, since the two touch the same number.
findings.test_first: tests/test_scoring_coverage_penalty.py::test_coverage_discount_is_continuous — for each category, sweep k from 1 to n and assert the ratio between consecutive spec_raw values never exceeds 1.15. Red at HEAD for 8/9 categories (fashion/fragrances worst at 1.4286).
findings.dedupe: known:M18/PO-rubric-02 — status FIXED/NOT-A-DEFECT as recorded (the 'inverted' claim does not hold; my independent arithmetic agrees with the M18 closeout). The step discontinuity is fresh.

findings.title: P3 sweep: session tab mapping still positional (6/9 categories wrong), trust-set parity confirmed clean, and five smaller rubric nits
findings.evidence: (1) SESSION TAB MAP — known:M18/PO-rubric-10, STILL-OPEN. apply_session_signals (:2795-2799) resolves tabs by dict position (dim_keys[0]/[2]/[3]). Enumerated all 9 categories against _DIMENSION_SIGNAL_MAP: 'reviews' dwell lands on a NON-review signal in 6/9 — electronics->build_quality_score (reliability), makeup->skin_compat_score (reliability), haircare->ingredient_score (reliability), fashion->style_score (popularity), supplements->dosage_score (spec_secondary), skincare->skin_compat_score (review, correct by luck); 'overview' (documented as a price/value proxy) lands on the value dim in only 3/9 (grocery, supplements, other) and on spec_secondary or reliability in the other 6. Only grocery and `other` are fully correct. (2) TRUST SET — known:#104, FIXED, verified: len(price_service._GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS)==15, len(_PRICE_TRUST_SET)==15, both set-differences EMPTY; measured price-authority behavior is correct in 126/126 provenance runs (genuine never loses to an estimate: page_scrape_jsonld 64.0 vs estimated 60.0; local_bhd 64.0 vs converted_usd 62.0, i.e. exactly -4.0 and -2.0 as _DEFAULT_PRICE_AUTHORITY_POINTS / _CONVERTED_USD_PENALTY_RATIO specify). (3) A product with NO price object at all takes the full -4.0 estimate-grade penalty (_product_source_method :720-724 defaults to 'estimated'), so 'no price' and 'GPT-guessed price' are punished identically. (4) The collapse guards at :2113/:2122/:2145 skip collapsing when the tied value happens to equal 50.0 exactly (`!= MISSING_SCORE`), so a genuine reliability_raw of exactly 0.5 on both sides is treated as real while 0.51 is treated as phantom. (5) compute_scores derives `category` from products_data[0] only (:1288), so a mixed-category pair is scored entirely on product 0's rubric. (6) build_scores_summary (:2836-2842) re-derives the category by matching the breakdown key set instead of reading the `category` key compute_scores now returns (:1567). (7) _empty_result (:2411-2428) returns scoring_method 'default', a value not in the documented enum the label branch at :1524-1542 produces.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/porubric/p2.py — sections 'apply_session_signals TAB -> DIM POSITIONAL MAP', 'PRICE TRUST SET PARITY', and gen.py/an.py section 'PRICE PROVENANCE'.
findings.impact: (1) a user reading reviews is nudged toward build quality or brand popularity — the +/-5% layer moves the wrong dimension in two thirds of categories, so any session-personalization measurement is measuring noise. (2)/(3) informational: #104 can be closed, but the no-price case deserves its own delta so 'we have no price' is not scored as 'we guessed a price'. (4)-(7) latent inconsistencies with no live user impact today.
findings.fix: (1) Replace the positional guesses with a signal lookup, exactly as M18 PO-rubric-10 prescribes: build tab_dim_map from _DIMENSION_SIGNAL_MAP — 'specs' -> the dim whose signal is 'spec', 'reviews' -> 'review', 'overview' -> 'value' — falling back to no-op when a category has no such dim. (2) Close #104 and keep tests/test_price_trust_set_parity.py as the ratchet. (3) Add a distinct, smaller `_NO_PRICE_PENALTY` (or 0 with an explicit 'price unavailable' surface) instead of reusing the estimate delta. (4) Drop the `!= MISSING_SCORE` co-condition once PO-RUBRIC-02's sparsity gate replaces the blanket collapse. (5) Canonicalize per product and fall back to 'other' when the two disagree. (6) Read scoring_result['category']. (7) Return 'category_weighted' from _empty_result or add 'default' to the documented enum.
findings.test_first: tests/test_session_signals.py::test_tab_dwell_moves_the_signal_it_names — parametrize over all 9 categories; for tab_dwell_ms={'reviews': 10000, 'specs': 1}, assert the dim whose weight increased is the one _DIMENSION_SIGNAL_MAP marks 'review'. Red at HEAD in 6/9 categories.
findings.dedupe: (1) known:M18/PO-rubric-10 still-open (fresh: exact per-category mapping table, 6/9 wrong, and 'overview' also wrong in 6/9); (2) known:#104 FIXED (verified parity, both differences empty); (3)-(7) new, P3.

{context}

</SEARCH_RESULTS>

findings.impact: OPENAI_MODEL_STANDARD is the knob an operator would reach for under cost or TPM pressure — it covers parsing, specs, price, reviews, Tier-2/Tier-3 fills and the critic, i.e. every call in a compare except the verdict. Setting it to any gpt-5 id 400s 11 of those sites instantly ('Only the default (1) value is supported' / 'max_tokens is not supported'), which is a total compare outage with a green deploy and no code change to blame. findings.title: Internal scoring-dimension values ship to users in pros/cons: four recorded production strings defeat the HEAD scrubber has_score_internals
findings.evidence: Ran the REAL app.services.text_sanitize.has_score_internals from 76ace90 over 282 pros+cons strings from the 26 recorded Supabase comparisons: 33 mention a score/point/rank concept, 13 caught (item dropped by response_builder.py:1558-1563), 20 missed. Four of the misses are genuine internal-score leaks: 'Performance score is only 30.0, lower than competitors.', 'Build quality score is slightly lower at 90.9.', 'Build quality score is only 40.0', 'Build quality score is relatively low at 35.0.' Direct call: has_score_internals('Performance score is only 30.0, lower than competitors.') = False, strip_score_internals(...) returns the string UNCHANGED. _SCORE_PATTERNS (text_sanitize.py:7-20) matches 'score of N', 'scores N', 'N points', '/100', 'overall score', '+Npt', 'deviation of N%' — none of which covers the 'X score is [adverb] {at|only} N' shape. 'performance' and 'build_quality' are exactly CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS breakdown keys.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/m22-review/po-prompts/scrub.py — read-only Supabase SELECT of comparisons.full_response, then app.services.text_sanitize.has_score_internals (imported from the repo at HEAD) applied to every pros/cons string. No network beyond the Supabase read.
findings.impact: COMPARISON_SYSTEM:1042 bans this absolutely ('NEVER mention internal scores, point margins, "/100" values, "overall score", or any "N-point"/"score of N" phrasing in ANY field — this includes ... pros, cons ... Those internal scores are NEVER shown to the user'). Both the prompt ban and the defence-in-depth scrubber fail on the same shape, so the user reads '/Performance score is only 30.0/' as if it were a product fact — a meaningless 0-100 internal number presented as a reason not to buy. 4 leaks in 282 strings from 26 comparisons; the model that produced them is the mid-June engine, but the SCRUBBER that misses them is at HEAD, so the defence gap is current regardless.
findings.fix: Add two patterns to _SCORE_PATTERNS in app/services/text_sanitize.py:7-20 — `re.compile(r"\\bscores?\\s+(?:is|are|of|at)?\\s*(?:only|just|relatively|slightly)?\\s*(?:lower|higher|low|high)?\\s*(?:at|of)?\\s*\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?", re.I)` for the 'score is only N' / 'score is slightly lower at N' family, and a dimension-anchored one built from CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS keys so a new phrasing on a known dimension is caught structurally rather than lexically. Better still, invert the defence: since scoring dimensions are a closed set, drop any pros/cons item containing a CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS name within N tokens of a bare decimal. Unflagged — this only drops items the prompt already forbids.
findings.test_first: tests/test_text_sanitize.py::test_recorded_score_leaks_are_caught — parametrize the four literal production strings above and assert has_score_internals(s) is True for each. Red at HEAD on all four. Pair it with a negative case asserting 'High user rating of 4.7 from 54,000 reviews' stays False, since that is a legitimate retailer rating and must not be dropped.

findings.title: STATUS still-open, now measured: the never-empty-cons rule turns pipeline data gaps into product criticism in 8% of shipped cons, and the model disobeys it anyway 15% of the time
findings.evidence: COMPARISON_SYSTEM:1030 — 'NEVER return empty pros[] or cons[] arrays — every product has SOME observable strengths and weaknesses ... If two products feel close to identical, surface what makes each one distinctive in PRACTICAL use, even small differences.' Measured over 113 cons strings in the 26 recorded comparisons: 9 (8%) criticise the pipeline's own data gap rather than the product — 'Limited information on longevity.', 'Limited information on specific scent notes.', 'No details on longevity or season suitability.', 'Limited information on scent longevity and sillage.', 'Limited information on material and origin.', 'No specific material or origin information', 'No specific cons noted in reviews' (x3). Six of the nine are TOM FORD fragrances, where longevity/sillage/notes_*/material/origin are exactly the schema fields the specs cascade routinely leaves blank. Separately, 8 of 52 product sides shipped an EMPTY cons[] despite the absolute rule.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/m22-review/po-prompts/cons.py (data-gap regex over the recorded cons) and scratchpad/m22-review/po-prompts/sb2.py (empty-cons count). Read-only Supabase SELECT.
findings.impact: A user comparing two Tom Ford perfumes reads 'Limited information on longevity' as a fact about the perfume. It is a fact about Qaren — the app is confessing its own extraction miss in the product's own con list, on the exact category where the fragrance schema is thinnest. The 15% empty-cons rate is the same defect's other face: the rule is absolute enough to manufacture filler when obeyed and is disobeyed anyway, so it buys nothing. Rows are ≤2026-06-21 (mid-June engine), but the prompt line is unchanged at HEAD.
findings.fix: Make the rule evidence-conditional the way #111 already made the nine personality evidence_language entries: replace the 'NEVER return empty' absolute with 'Return a con ONLY when the supplied product data supports one. If the data genuinely shows no weakness for a product, return an empty cons[] — an honest empty list is correct, and a con about MISSING DATA ("limited information on X", "no details on Y") is NEVER acceptable: that describes our data, not the product.' Belt-and-braces at the seam: add a data-gap regex to text_sanitize alongside has_score_internals and drop matching items in the same response_builder.py:1558-1563 filter that already drops score leaks. Ship the prompt change behind the existing ENABLE_COMPARISON_QUALITY_V2 if you want it to land with the rest of the honest-thin-evidence work; the scrubber half needs no flag.

Plus tests/test_verdict_prompt.py asserting 'NEVER return empty pros[] or cons[]' is absent from the rendered verdict prompt. Both red at HEAD.

findings.title: The rendered verdict prompt both bans and mandates talking about internal scores — two rules from two files contradict inside one system message
findings.evidence: build_verdict_prompt appends build_personality_prompt (extraction_service.py:1990) to COMPARISON_SYSTEM, so UNIVERSAL_TRUST_RULES and the score ban land in the SAME string. Measured on the rendered prompt: 'score-mention contradiction: ban_line=True trustrule_scores=True'. COMPARISON_SYSTEM:1042 — 'NEVER mention internal scores, point margins, "/100" values, "overall score", or any "N-point"/"score of N" phrasing in ANY field ... Those internal scores are NEVER shown to the user'. prompt_personalities.py:73 — 'NO overconfidence: if data is thin or scores are close (<5 point gap), say "marginally" or "slightly"'; :77 — 'If scores disagree with your intuition, explain why (do not silently ignore scores)'. Line 77 orders the model to EXPLAIN a score disagreement in its output, which is only possible by referencing the scores line 1042 forbids. Line 76 ('CITE the data: every claim must reference a specific spec, rating, or review finding') also contradicts :1030's 'NEVER return empty cons[]' whenever no such data exists.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/m22-review/po-prompts/render.py — calls the real extraction_service.build_verdict_prompt(products=..., comparison_quality='normal', category='electronics') and greps the single returned string for both clauses. Static; no OpenAI call possible.
findings.impact: An LLM given a hard NEVER and a hard MUST over the same subject resolves it arbitrarily and inconsistently, which is the most plausible upstream cause of the score leaks measured in PO-PROMPTS-04 ('Performance score is only 30.0, lower than competitors.' is exactly what rule 77 asks for and rule 1042 forbids). The contradiction is invisible in review because the two halves live in different files and only meet at assembly time.
findings.fix: Rewrite UNIVERSAL_TRUST_RULES lines 73 and 77 so the score stays an INPUT and never an output token: :73 -> 'NO overconfidence: when the supplied data is thin or the two products are close, say "marginally" or "slightly" — describe the closeness in plain words, never as a number'; :77 -> 'If the supplied scores disagree with your reading of the product facts, follow the product facts and say which fact drove you — do NOT mention, quote or allude to the scores themselves.' Also reconcile :76 with COMPARISON_SYSTEM:1030 by adopting PO-PROMPTS-05's conditional wording. Unflagged prompt-text-only change; add a contradiction guard test so the two files cannot drift apart again.
