findings.title: is_supplement_query runs before the category synonyms, so a topical vitamin-C serum and topical minoxidil are classified as supplements and asked for their dosage and serving size
findings.evidence: extraction_service.py:1170-1173 — `classify_category_from_text` calls `is_supplement_query(text)` FIRST and returns 'supplements' on a hit, before the synonym sweep at :1175-1179 ever sees 'serum' or 'skin'. `is_supplement_query` (price_service.py:1181-1182 at 76ace90) returns True on any UNAMBIGUOUS token standing alone; its own docstring exempts 'collagen serum' (via the AMBIGUOUS list) but 'vitamin c' has no such guard. Measured over 360 queries: 'expected=skincare got=supplements: Vitamin C serum Skinceuticals CE Ferulic vs Timeless 20%'; 'expected=skincare got=supplements: Garnier Vitamin C serum vs Loreal Revitalift'; 'expected=haircare got=supplements: Minoxidil 5% Kirkland vs Rogaine foam'.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/lane/run_gate.py — the REAL `classify_category_from_text` over the corpus; the wrong-category block is reproduced identically by the real `_resolve_pair_category` in run_resolve.py.
findings.impact: Vitamin-C serum and sunscreen/retinol comparisons are among the highest-volume GCC skincare queries. Misrouted to supplements, they are scored on efficacy 0.30 / safety 0.25 / dosage 0.15 (scoring_service.py:68) and extracted against the supplements schema (count, serving_size, active_ingredient, dosage, form, allergens, certifications, shelf_life, calories) — so the 'At a glance' block asks a face serum for its serving size and calorie count and the Specs table shows N/A for most rows, while the fairness like-for-like axis silently becomes 'unit count' instead of ml. Because of PO-CATEGORIES-I18N-04 this also overrides a user who explicitly tapped the Skincare chip.
findings.fix: Add a topical-form veto to `is_supplement_query`: if the name contains a topical form token (serum, cream, lotion, gel, ointment, foam, toner, cleanser, shampoo, mask, spray-for-hair, topical, %-strength-on-a-cosmetic) and no supplement FORM token (capsule/tablet/softgel/gummy/powder/sachet), return False — the same corroboration discipline the AMBIGUOUS branch already uses, applied as a negative signal. Alternatively reorder `classify_category_from_text` so an explicit skincare/haircare synonym hit wins over the supplement heuristic. Ship behind ENABLE_TOPICAL_SUPPLEMENT_VETO; flag-off is byte-identical. Note `is_supplement_query` is also consulted by the price path, so measure both.
findings.test_first: `test_topical_actives_are_not_supplements`: `classify_category_from_text('Vitamin C serum Skinceuticals CE Ferulic vs Timeless 20%') == 'skincare'` and `classify_category_from_text('Minoxidil 5% Kirkland vs Rogaine foam') == 'haircare'`, alongside a green-today guard that `classify_category_from_text('Vitamin C 1000mg effervescent Redoxon vs Cevit') == 'supplements'`.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: The copy-policy fence audits only the two i18n catalogs, so 12 backend strings carrying the banned 'Failed to' / 'try again' vocabulary ship to clients unchecked
findings.evidence: copy-policy.test.ts:46-48 imports exactly `../src/i18n/en.json`, `../src/i18n/ar.json` and the policy — nothing else is scanned. Sweeping the same `scary_vocab_en` list (['couldn't','try again','Failed to']) over every `"error"/"detail"/"message"` string literal under app/ at 76ace90 yields 12 hits: auth_routes.py:886 'Failed to register push token'; auth_routes.py:973 'Failed to update notification preferences'; referral_routes.py:222 'Too many shares — please try again later.'; share_routes.py:39 'Failed to create share link'; auth_service.py:53 'Connection failed. Please try again.'; :68 'Something went wrong. Please try again later.'; :224 'Failed to refresh session'; :470 'Failed to load preferences'; :515 'Failed to save preferences'; database_service.py:595 'Failed to save demographics'; :633 'Failed to save attribution'; url_extraction_service.py:435 'Failed to fetch URL'. Catalog side is clean (0 scary hits in 896 keys x 2 locales). The backend even documents the contract it is violating (response_builder.py:684, scs.py:1439).
findings.repro: python scratchpad/lane/partd.py — loads the real .copy-policy.json and walks every .py under app/, matching quoted error/detail/message literals. Report: scratchpad/lane/partd_report.txt.
findings.impact: These reach a client the same way the compare errors do. Auth flows are the known hole (M18 MB-flows-11 P3: 'every error path renders raw axios/backend English'), so a failed session refresh or preference save shows 'Failed to refresh session' — English, in the banned register, to an Arabic user. The deeper issue is that the fence gives false assurance: it goes green on every CI build while the backend, which produces the strings users actually see on failure, is never audited.
findings.fix: Extend the fence rather than the copy. Add a second describe block to copy-policy.test.ts (or a pytest equivalent in tests/) that reads .copy-policy.json and scans backend client-facing literals, with an explicit allowlist file for strings that are logs-only. Then give each of the 12 sites a `code` and let the client substitute — the CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE / TIMEOUT pattern already in api.ts:849-908 is the template. No flag: adding codes is additive.
findings.test_first: The new fence itself is the red test — it fails today on 12 strings. Pair it with an api.ts test asserting each new code maps to a catalog key that exists in BOTH locales.
findings.dedupe: new (the fence's blind spot); the auth-screen rendering half is known:M18/MB-flows-11 still-open

findings.title: Two screens format the same price two different ways, and the unpinned toLocaleString() leaks Arabic-Indic digits into English copy on an ar-locale device
findings.evidence: ResultsContent.tsx:143 `${localizedCurrency(price.currency, t)} ${price.amount.toLocaleString()}` — code FIRST, no locale argument, no fraction digits. ResultsScreen.tsx:411 is the same shape. HistoryScreen.tsx:715 `${product.price.amount.toFixed(2)} ${localizedCurrency(product.price.currency || 'BHD', t)}` — code LAST, always 2 decimals, always Latin digits. `localizedCurrency` (currencyDisplay.ts:17-25) resolves `currency.BHD` to 'BHD' in EN and 'د.ب' in AR, so the glyph follows the APP language while the digits follow the DEVICE locale — the two can disagree in both directions.
findings.repro: static, read at 76ace90 (SmartCompareApp/ is unchanged from 76ace90 in the current worktree). `Number.prototype.toLocaleString()` with no argument uses the runtime's default locale, which on an ar-BH device is ar — producing '١٢٫٥' — while the app language may be English. Not observed on a device (no device in this environment).
findings.impact: Three distinct defects on the same value. (a) An English-language app on an ar-locale phone renders 'BHD ١٢٫٥' — Arabic-Indic digits inside English copy. (b) BHD's 3-decimal convention is lost everywhere: Results shows '12.5', History shows '12.50'; neither is '12.500'. (c) The same comparison shows 'BHD 12.5' on Results and '12.50 BHD' in History, which in RTL puts the currency on opposite sides of the number on two screens of one app. M21's localizedCurrency fixed the glyph half of M18 MB-i18n-rtl-07 and left the digit and decimal halves open.
findings.fix: One shared formatter in currencyDisplay.ts — `formatPrice(amount, code, t, language)` — that pins the numeral system to the APP language (`new Intl.NumberFormat(language === 'ar' ? 'ar-u-nu-latn' : 'en-US', {minimumFractionDigits: DECIMALS[code] ?? 2, maximumFractionDigits: DECIMALS[code] ?? 2})` with `DECIMALS = {BHD:3, KWD:3, OMR:3}`) and fixes one order for the code+amount pair. Replace all three call sites. Decide the Arabic-Indic question deliberately: pinning `-u-nu-latn` is the safest default for prices and matches the majority of ar.json values (M18 MB-i18n-rtl-06 measured 20 Western vs 32 Arabic-Indic). No flag needed; it is presentation-only.
findings.test_first: `currencyDisplay.test.ts`: with i18n language 'ar' and a mocked device locale of 'ar-BH', assert `formatPrice(12.5,'BHD',t,'ar')` returns Latin digits with exactly 3 decimals; and assert Results and History produce byte-identical strings for the same {amount, currency}. Red today on both.
findings.dedupe: known:M18/MB-i18n-rtl-07 — PARTIALLY FIXED at HEAD (currencyDisplay.ts landed in M21 W4 and fixes the glyph half); the digit-system, decimal-precision and cross-screen-order halves are still open, with fresh evidence

findings.title: P3 sweep: 6 smaller category/i18n defects found while checking every cell
findings.evidence: (1) MISLABELLED ALIAS — extraction_service.py:250 `"electronics.washer": {"dimensions": "weight"}` writes the washer's physical dimension string into the canonical `weight` field, so the Specs table and 'At a glance' render e.g. 'Weight: 600 x 850 x 600 mm' under the i18n label results.spec.weight. electronics has no `dimensions` field, so the alias was the only way to keep the value — but the label is now a lie. (2) DEAD TRANSLATED STRING — `results.categorySwitched` exists in en.json:851 AND ar.json:848 and is wired on the response (response_builder.py:1679, types.ts:296), yet ResultsScreen.tsx:774 deleted the banner and __tests__/ResultsScreen.bundleE.s3.test.tsx:154 asserts the source never references it. (3) AR PLURALS PARTIAL — measured over ar.json: 6 plural bases; `history.hero.count` and `home.savings.count` now carry all 6 Arabic forms (zero/one/two/few/many/other) but `referrals.bonus.expiresInDays`, `expiresInHours`, `expiresInMinutes` still carry only `_one`/`_other`, so Arabic counts 0, 2, 3-10 and 11-99 fall to the wrong form. (4) KEYWORD FALSE POSITIVES beyond the supplement case: 'Prayer mat electronic vs Sajjadah normal' -> electronics (the synonym 'electronic' matches an adjective), 'Perfume oil burner electric vs mabkhara traditional' -> fragrances (a mabkhara is a burner, not a perfume), 'Lock and Lock food container 1L vs Tupperware 1L' -> grocery — the last is verbatim the FIX-1 example scs.py:326-327 says was fixed, still broken on the explicit_pair path. (5) NON-DETERMINISTIC META ORDER — extraction_service.py:1489 `for key in list(meta_keys) + ...` iterates a set literal, so brand/model/variant/category order varies per process; harmless today only because ResultsAccordion.tsx:77 HIDDEN_FIELDS drops all four. (6) SPECS-TABLE LABEL FALLBACK — ResultsAccordion.tsx:584 falls back to `key.replace(/_/g,' ')`, so any non-canonical key that ever reaches the client renders as a raw lowercase snake key in both locales (CategoryProfile.tsx:138 at least falls back to the backend's humanized English label).
findings.repro: Items (1),(2),(5),(6) static at 76ace90. Items (3),(4) measured: scratchpad/lane/run_gate.py (real classify_category_from_text over 360 queries) and a scripted plural-suffix census of ar.json.
findings.impact: Individually small. (1) shows a wrong label on every washing-machine comparison — a mainstream GCC category. (3) gives Arabic users wrong grammar on referral-expiry copy. (4) sends three plausible query shapes to the wrong schema and dimension set. (2),(5),(6) are latent.
findings.fix: (1) Either add `dimensions` to CATEGORY_SPEC_SCHEMAS['electronics'] plus the matching `results.spec.dimensions` key (which already exists in both catalogs, because the 'other' schema has the field) and drop the alias, or retarget the alias to a field whose label is honest. (2) Render the string or delete it from both catalogs and the wire. (3) Add zero/two/few/many to the three referral bases. findings.title: Serper-shopping rung parses the Bahraini "BD" display token with no currency and ships 22.500 BD as 22500 BHD (1000x), stamped local_bhd
findings.evidence: detect_currency reads CURRENCY_SYMBOLS ({$,£,€,¥}) + CURRENCY_CODES (11 ISO) only, never GCC_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS which maps "BD"->BHD. Measured: `22.500 BD  detect=None parse=22500.0 | OFF amt=22500.0 cur=BHD sm=local_bhd | ON amt=22500.0 sm=local_bhd`. Shipped dict: showable=True, ttl=604800, trust=True.
findings.repro: python anz9.py (scratchpad/po-price, head76 tree, PROD flags): ps.extract_price_from_shopping('Lattafa Khamrah Eau de Parfum 100ml', [{'title':...,'price':'22.500 BD','source':'Noon','link':'https://www.noon.com/uae-en/p/x'}], 'BHD', None, 'fragrances') -> {'amount': 22500.0, 'currency': 'BHD', 'source_method': 'local_bhd'}; is_price_showable(..., enforce_correctness=True)=True; price_cache_ttl=604800.
findings.impact: A native BAHRAINI shelf price written the way Bahraini stores write it (BD 22.500) is served as 22,500 BHD - a 1000x overstatement - labelled a genuine local price, cached 7 days, and given ZERO price-authority penalty in scoring (_PRICE_TRUST_SET). It is the home currency's own notation, so it is the most likely string to hit. ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY (the M13-09 dark fix) does NOT catch it: _shopping_foreign_currency_signal resolves the residue "BD" to the TARGET currency and correctly declines to pend, but the amount was already parsed with currency=None so parse_price_string treated the '.' as a thousands group. Latent today only because the Serper account balance is negative; SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 is the gate's explicit OFF switch (api_budget_service.py:94), i.e. Serper is UNGATED, not disabled - funding the key ships this immediately.
findings.fix: Resolve the shopping token through the GCC-aware resolver before parsing, not only in the pend guard: at price_service.py:9572 replace `detected_cur = detect_currency(price_str)` with a resolution that falls back to _normalize_currency_code on the number-stripped residue (the same residue _shopping_foreign_currency_signal already computes at :9457-9458), then pass that code into parse_price_string at :9584 so parse-currency == stamped-currency by construction - exactly the M13-08 rule already applied to the WooCommerce span at :13396. Ship behind the existing ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY (it is already the shopping rung's currency-label flag and is already default OFF), and extend shopping_strict_currency_pend so an unresolvable residue pends rather than parses.
findings.test_first: tests/test_shopping_currency_display_tokens.py: parametrize ('22.500 BD',22.5),('8.750 KD',10.7625),('250 SR',25.075),('32,000 QR',3305.6) through extract_price_from_shopping with currency='BHD' and assert amount == expected and source_method == ('local_bhd' for BD else 'converted_usd'); a red run today returns 22500.0/8750.0/250.0/32000.0 all stamped local_bhd.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: Shopping rung stamps TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/DKK/CAD amounts as unconverted BHD local_bhd, and ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY does not pend them either
findings.evidence: CURRENCY_CODES (:546-550) holds 11 ISO codes; TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/DKK/CAD/EGP/JOD are absent, so detect_currency returns None, item_converted stays False and the raw number is stamped currency=BHD/local_bhd. Measured: `TRY 1.299,00 detect=None parse=1299.0 | OFF amt=1299.0 cur=BHD sm=local_bhd | ON amt=1299.0 sm=local_bhd`; same for `PLN 249,00` and `CHF 64.30`.
findings.repro: python anz9.py at head76 with PROD flags and then ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY=true: both modes return {'amount': 1299.0, 'currency': 'BHD', 'source_method': 'local_bhd'} for price_str='TRY 1.299,00'. _shopping_foreign_currency_signal('TRY 1.299,00','BHD') is False because _normalize_currency_code('TRY') is None (TRY is not in effective_fallback_rates with ENABLE_EXTENDED_FALLBACK_RATES off) and the residue 'TRY' is pure ASCII, so the :9468 non-ASCII catch-all never fires.
findings.impact: TRY 1,299 (~12 BHD) ships as 1,299 BHD - a 108x overstatement - as a GENUINE Bahrain price with the 7-day genuine TTL and no authority penalty. The corpus proves the exposure is real, not theoretical: 35 of the 414 cached pages are priced in TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/DKK/CAD/EGP/JOD retailers (sephora.com.tr, kicks.se, matas.dk, perfumeria.pl, eperfumy.pl, douglas.ch, fragrancecanada.ca, smartbuy-me.com), and those are exactly the retailers Serper shopping surfaces for a global fragrance query. Worse than 01 because the two currency guards are structurally coupled to the SAME 13-entry rate table: a currency absent from FALLBACK_RATES is simultaneously unconvertible and undetectable-as-foreign, so it fails open into the local-currency label.
findings.fix: Break the coupling: the foreign-signal test must not depend on convertibility. In _shopping_foreign_currency_signal (:9462) treat a residue that is a well-formed 3-letter ISO alpha code but is NOT the target as FOREIGN even when _normalize_currency_code returns None - an unconvertible foreign currency must pend, never inherit the target label. Pair it with ENABLE_EXTENDED_FALLBACK_RATES so the ten corpus currencies convert instead of pending (see PO-PRICE-TRUTH-10, which measures that flip as purely additive). Both behind ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY; the pend half is safe to ship first.
findings.test_first: tests/test_shopping_foreign_iso_pend.py: with ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY=true and ENABLE_EXTENDED_FALLBACK_RATES=false, assert extract_price_from_shopping(q,[{'price':'TRY 1.299,00',...}],'BHD') is None for each of TRY/PLN/CHF/SEK/DKK/CAD/EGP/JOD/ZAR/MYR; today every one returns the raw number stamped local_bhd.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: The sample/decant guard is fed price['title'], but every extract_price_from_html branch stamps the listing identity as price['name'] - so the guard is blind on the entire page-scrape rung
findings.evidence: is_price_showable :1694 `title = price.get("title")` then :1722 `if _is_sample_or_decant_listing(product_name, title, amount)`. The JSON-LD/OG/microdata branches stamp only `result["name"]` (:13185, :12967). Measured: _is_sample_or_decant_listing('Xerjoff Ilm Eau de Parfum', "'Ilm Sample & Decants by Xerjoff", 94.0)=True but =False when title is None. Three sibling guards at :8813/:8853/:8894 already use `price.get("title") or price.get("name")`.
findings.repro: python anz6.py at head76, PROD flags: the scentsplit capture {'amount':94.0,'source_method':'converted_usd','name':"'Ilm Sample & Decants by Xerjoff", no 'title'} gives is_price_showable(...,enforce_correctness=True)=True with sample_guard=False. python anz7.py shows the same string passed as `title` returns True. Corpus source: _proof/global/html for https://scentsplit.com/products/xerjoff-ilm-sample-decants (page's own JSON-LD names: "'Ilm - 1ml Sample", "'Ilm - 2ml Glass Spray", "'Ilm - 50ml in Manufacturer's bottle").
findings.impact: Every price produced by the page-scrape rung - 176 of 414 corpus pages at PROD flags, and the rung ENABLE_PAGE_SCRAPE=true keeps live in prod - reaches the display chokepoint with the sample/decant guard disarmed, because the M2 change that gave those branches an identity chose the key `name` while the chokepoint reads `title`. A listing whose own name says 'Sample & Decants', '1ml Sample' or 'decant vial' is shown as the product's price. The same silent-empty-string bug also blanks the L2 content-safety surface at scs.py:1660 (`price.get('title','')`), so an unsafe listing name is never seen there either.
findings.fix: One line at price_service.py:1694: `title = price.get("title") or price.get("name")`, matching the idiom already used three times in the same module (:8813/:8853/:8894). No flag is warranted - it can only make the chokepoint stricter, and the guard it re-arms is one the codebase already ships. Do the same at scs.py:1660 for the safety surface. Then audit the other `price.get("title")` readers for the same key drift.

findings.title: The JSON-LD multiplicity pend ("never a silent pick") is bypassed by the OG branch: 13 of 16 multi-variant captures ship whatever og:price:amount says, i.e. Shopify's default variant
findings.evidence: extract_price_from_html sets _multiplicity_pend when the ladder returns candidates, but _finish (:13047) only stamps CAPTURE_AMBIGUOUS_PRICE `if price is None and _multiplicity_pend` - and _extract_og_price at :13263 has already produced a price from a single meta tag with no variant awareness. Corpus: 52/414 pages carry >=2 distinct JSON-LD Offer amounts; 16 ship a price; picked = MIN 11 / MAX 4 / MID 1 - i.e. whatever the tag holds, never a size-aware choice.
findings.repro: python anz4.py over sweep_out.json (PROD flags, ask=BHD). Worked examples reproduced individually with anz3.py/anz5.py: yusufbhaifragrances.com/products/dior-sauvage - JSON-LD offers 70.00 AED ('YB Sauvage - 100ml') and 50.00 AED ('YB Sauvage - 50ml'), the BHD-leg ladder returns null with pending_out=[], og:price:amount=70.00, shipped 7.17 BHD conf=0.9 outcome='ok'. parfumgroup.de/products/dolce-gabbana-the-one-eau-de-parfum - 8 offers 40.99..71.99 EUR, shipped 29.52 BHD = the MAX (og 71,99), conf=0.675, price_confirmed_in_text=False. www.sephora.com/product/dior-sauvage-elixir-P475526 is the control: same multiplicity, NO og:price tag, and it correctly pends with outcome='ambiguous_price'.
findings.impact: On a multi-variant PDP the price the user sees is Shopify's default/first variant, chosen by a meta tag, and the pinned A3 multiplicity policy (query-size wins -> request context -> pend; never a silent pick) is enforced on exactly the pages that happen to omit og:price:amount. Both directions ship: parfumgroup ships the most expensive of 8 variants (71.99 EUR when the cheapest in-stock is 41.55), and www.indigoperfumery.com ships 1.50 BHD ($3.99, the sample) for '001 by Bon Parfumeur' whose full bottle on the same page is $60 - a 15x understatement that would hand indigoperfumery any value comparison. 4 of the 16 are MAX picks and 5 have a >=1.2x spread.
findings.fix: Make the multiplicity fact decisive for the whole cascade, not just the JSON-LD return: hoist _multiplicity_pend so that when the ladder handed back >1 distinct candidate amount and none was resolved, extract_price_from_html returns None BEFORE _extract_og_price/_extract_microdata_price/_extract_woocommerce_price run - the OG tag cannot discriminate a variant and must not be allowed to answer a question the ladder already declined. Ship behind a new default-OFF ENABLE_MULTIPLICITY_BLOCKS_FALLBACK: it converts 13 shipped prices into pends on this corpus, which is a capture-rate change and needs its own canary. Flag OFF is byte-identical (one bool read).

findings.title: 16 of 16 multi-variant captures ship with size=None because _stamp_listing_size is gated on is_fragrance_query(query), which is False for a fragrance whose query carries no fragrance word
findings.evidence: _stamp_listing_size :11121 `if not is_fragrance_query(product_name): return result`. Measured: is_fragrance_query('YB Sauvage')=False and is_fragrance_query('YB Sauvage 50ml')=False, so even when the extractor matches the right variant the size is dropped - `q='YB Sauvage 50ml' -> amount=5.12 size=None name='YB Sauvage - 50ml'`. Contrast `q='Chanel Coco Mademoiselle Crush Absolu Eau De Parfum 100ml' -> size=100ml`.
findings.repro: python anz5.py at head76 (PROD flags) over the cached yusufbhai/fenwick/scentsplit/goldencollections bodies; python anz4.py reports `shipped with NO size stamp: 16` out of 16 multi-offer captures, and 80 of the 132 fragrance-category captures corpus-wide carry no size.
findings.impact: The size the fairness engine needs is present in the page's own matched JSON-LD variant name ('YB Sauvage - 50ml', 'ج. ايرث للجنسين - 30 مل') and is thrown away because the gate asks whether the QUERY looks like a fragrance rather than whether the resolved category is one. A sizeless fragrance price is then handed the flagship-100ml basis by the pair reconcile, so a genuine 50ml at 5.12 BHD is compared as if it were a 100ml - a 2x value error in the winner computation, on the side of whichever retailer happens to default to the smaller bottle. The orchestrator already knows the real category (_resolved_category_ctx); the extractor asks the wrong oracle.
findings.fix: Gate on the RESOLVED category, not the query text: in extract_price_from_html the local `_category = _resolve_extractor_category(category, product_name)` is already computed at :13018 - thread it into _stamp_listing_size and use `_category == 'fragrances' or is_fragrance_query(product_name)` as the gate, and read the size from the matched JSON-LD variant name first (it is already passed as `jsonld_name`). Ship under the existing ENABLE_FRAGRANCE_SIZE_RECONCILE_FIX family or a sibling default-OFF flag, because adding a size where there was none changes pair-fairness outcomes.
findings.test_first: tests/test_size_stamp_uses_resolved_category.py: extract_price_from_html(yusufbhai_html,'YB Sauvage 50ml','BHD','yusufbhaifragrances.com',url,category='fragrances') must return size=='50ml'; red today (size absent).

Excluding the 13 probe queries: n=1,513 (11.4%), success 1,210 (80.0%), success-latency p50=21,954ms p90=29,540 p95=30,004 p99=30,637; failures are 167 timeout + 114 parse + 13 'Still gathering' + 7 'incomplete' + 2 category, and ZERO 'blocked' and ZERO 'We need a moment more'. get_daily_stats computes avg_duration_ms = sum(duration_ms)/total over all rows (78% of which are 0).
findings.repro: Read-only SELECT of search_logs since 2026-06-01 (13,237 rows) via supabase service key; scripts at scratchpad/po-rm/sl.py, sl3.py, zero.txt. Then open app/services/analytics_service.py:12-32 and :59-74 at 76ace90 — neither get_daily_stats nor get_popular_queries filters query text, user_id, or a synthetic-traffic marker.

findings.title: 1,214 of 1,484 cached prices stamped `local_bhd` (81.8%) are not on a Bahrain URL — 857 are a google.com Shopping search link — because the stamp is decided only by 'we did not convert', never by retailer country
findings.evidence: product_prices, all 3,945 rows, (source_method x url host): local_bhd + www.google.com = 857; local_bhd + <no url> = 168; local_bhd + uae.sharafdg.com = 55; local_bhd + www.extra.com (the /en-sa Saudi storefront) = 34; local_bhd + www.jarir.com = 11; local_bhd + www.virginmegastore.ae = 5. Genuinely BH-hosted local_bhd rows total ~270 of 1,484. The stamp at 9682 is `"source_method": "converted_usd" if item_converted else "local_bhd"` and item_converted (9591) is `region_is_us_fallback or bool(detected_cur and detected_cur != currency)` — there is no country, TLD or storefront check anywhere between 9562 and 9745. Recorded confirmation: 'Walmart - YYWireless' 259.44 and 'Best Buy' 514.43 both shipped `local_bhd` with confidence.price.method='retailer_verified'.
findings.repro: Read-only SELECT * FROM product_prices (3,945 rows) — scratchpad/po-rm/pp.py; cross-tab at pp.txt. Then read price_service.py:9562-9745 at 76ace90.
findings.impact: `local_bhd` is the strongest label in `_GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS` and is counted 1:1 by the genuine-BH-share KPI (eval_runner.py:390 pins the two sets equal). ~80% of that KPI's numerator is a US Google-Shopping listing or a UAE/Saudi storefront, so the headline 'genuine Bahrain price share' the activation gate reads is inflated by roughly 5x. Downstream, `is_price_showable` admits the method (1692) and the confidence pill renders 'retailer_verified', so where such a price is not caught by the URL guard the user is told a Walmart-US number is a verified Bahrain retail price.
findings.fix: Add a country predicate to the stamp: a candidate is `local_bhd` only when its resolved URL host is in the region's storefront set (source_router already carries per-host region data) OR the item currency was natively the region currency AND the host is not a search/aggregator domain; everything else becomes `converted_usd` (honest) or an unrecognized method. Ship behind ENABLE_REGION_SOURCED_LOCAL_LABEL so the KPI break is deliberate; publish the re-measured genuine-share the day it flips, because the number will fall hard and that fall is the fix working. Backfill/expire the 857 google.com-hosted local_bhd cache rows in the same change or the L2 cache keeps serving the old label.
findings.test_first: tests/test_local_bhd_requires_bh_host.py: call extract_price_from_shopping with a shopping item {source:'Best Buy', link:'https://www.google.com/search?ibp=oshop&q=x', price:'259.44'} at currency='BHD' and assert result['source_method'] != 'local_bhd'. RED at HEAD (returns local_bhd).
findings.dedupe: new — M13's 'currency-is-a-label' theme and #52 (iHerb currency tautology) cover the CONVERSION label; PO-FACTCHECK-CONFIDENCE-04/#106 covers verify_price certifying a wrong-currency amount. Neither covers the genuine-BH stamp being blind to retailer country, and none has the 3,945-row measurement. still-open

findings.title: The shopping tier writes Serper's Google-Shopping search link into price.url, and HEAD's own chokepoint then pends it as non_pdp_url — replaying the recorded corpus, 24 of 40 priced cells self-pend and only 2 survive
findings.evidence: price_service.py:9678 `"url": item.get("link") or build_retailer_url(retailer, product_name)`. Serper shopping `link` is `https://www.google.com/search?ibp=oshop&q=...`; `build_retailer_url`'s fallback table (260-275) is entirely SEARCH templates (amazon /s?k=, walmart /search?q=, bestbuy searchpage.jsp, noon /search?q=). is_price_showable's backstop (1744-1746) does `if url and _is_listing_url(url): guard_rejected='non_pdp_url'; return False`, and exact_gate_enabled() defaults true (4093) and is NOT overridden in the Railway `web` vars. Replay of the 40 recorded priced cells through the real function: SHOWN=2, PEND=38, of which 24 are exactly `non_pdp_url`. is_non_pdp_listing_url returns True for all 6 recorded URL shapes and False only for the 2 tomford.com PDPs.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/po-rm/t_url.py — imports app.services.price_service.is_price_showable and app.services.source_router.is_non_pdp_listing_url from the working tree (both byte-identical to 76ace90 per `git diff 76ace90..HEAD`), feeds the 40 recorded price dicts. Output at scratchpad/po-rm/t_url.txt.
findings.impact: The Serper-Google-Shopping tier produced 26 of the 31 recorded prices that ever carried a URL — it is the highest-volume price source in the product — and at HEAD its output is structurally unshowable: the tier hands the chokepoint a URL the chokepoint is written to reject. The user gets the 'pricing lands soon' card on the tier that does most of the work, while the request still pays the Serper call and 6.5-15.9s of price_ms (measured, finding 13). This is the mechanism behind the pend surface, and it is invisible in the outcome series because a pend still logs success=True.
findings.fix: Stop putting a search URL in the shown price's `url`. Either (a) resolve the Serper shopping item to its merchant PDP before selection and drop candidates that cannot be resolved, or (b) keep the search link in a separate `discovery_url` field for diagnostics and leave `price['url']` unset — an absent URL is NOT pended by the backstop (1755 only pends when there is neither identity NOR url), so a candidate carrying `title` still displays. Option (b) is the one-line, no-network fix and should ship first behind ENABLE_SHOPPING_DISCOVERY_URL_SPLIT; option (a) is the real answer. Measure the pend rate before and after — this is the single largest lever on the shown-price rate.
findings.test_first: tests/test_shopping_price_not_self_pending.py: build a shopping candidate through extract_price_from_shopping with a google.com/search?ibp=oshop link and a matching title, then assert is_price_showable(name, price, cat, enforce_correctness=True) is True. RED at HEAD (False, guard_rejected='non_pdp_url').
findings.dedupe: new — the exact gate and _is_listing_url are documented as an intentional backstop; nobody has measured that the dominant price tier is the thing the backstop rejects. Not in M18/M13/mobile-checkup and not in the 33 open issues. still-open

findings.title: The winner and every dimension score are computed from the raw price, and the chokepoint pends that price afterwards — a recorded payload asserts a 24.4-point win and value_score 100.0 while shipping both prices as unavailable
findings.evidence: Order at HEAD: structured_comparison_service.py:3418 `scoring_result = scoring_service.compute_scores(product_data, ...)` runs on the raw product_data; build_comparison_response is called at :3557 and only there, at response_builder.py:1522, does `if not is_price_showable(_name, _price, _cat, enforce_correctness=True)` replace the amount with make_pending_price. Recorded proof, row 2a5d828d (2026-06-17, fragrances): both products carry `price = {amount: None, currency: 'BHD', unavailable: True, reason: ...}`, yet `overview.winner.reason` = 'TOM FORD BLACK ORCHID 100 ml wins with a 24.4 point higher score', scoring.scores.product_0.breakdown.value_score = 100.0, and `overview.confidence.legs.price` = 'acceptable' with `confidence.price.source_count` = 2. Row 640d483d: 1 of 2 products has NO price object at all and legs.price reads 'strong'. Row 779200c0: both unavailable, legs.price 'weak', source_count 0, verdict still declares a winner by 11.5 points.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/audit1.py + quant.py over the 27 rows (see the 'CONFIDENCE PRICE LEG vs ACTUAL PRICED CELLS' table in quant.txt); then read structured_comparison_service.py:3373-3392/3418 and response_builder.py:1494-1544 at 76ace90.
findings.impact: The two dimensions the user is most likely to act on (value, price) are decided by a number the product's own correctness gate has judged unfit to show, and the payload then presents the resulting margin as a fact. With finding 03 in play this is not a rare path — 24 of 40 recorded priced cells are pended AFTER scoring at HEAD, so the common case is a confidently-worded verdict whose price evidence was silently withdrawn from the same response. The comment at price_service.py:2992 already names this exact hazard for the region-currency half ('the chokepoint runs AFTER compute_scores has already picked a winner from the raw amount') and fixed it with a pre-scoring pass — the same fix was never applied to the correctness gate.
findings.fix: Mirror what apply_region_currency_guard did for M13-11: add a pre-scoring pass in the orchestrator, immediately after reconcile_pair_fairness (structured_comparison_service.py:3373) and before compute_scores (:3418), that runs is_price_showable(..., enforce_correctness=True) over product_data and pends in place, so the price and value dimensions take their honest missing-data path and the verdict prompt never sees the amount. Keep response_builder:1522 as the idempotent backstop for direct build_comparison_response callers (share/history rebuilds). Ship behind ENABLE_PRESCORING_SHOWABLE_GUARD; expect winner flips, which is the point.
findings.test_first: tests/test_prescoring_showable_guard.py: build two products whose prices carry a google.com search url (non_pdp_url), run the sync compare path with a stubbed LLM, assert scoring_result['scores']['product_0']['missing_data'] contains 'value_score' and that overview.winner.reason does not contain a price-derived margin. RED at HEAD (value_score is populated from the pended amount).
findings.dedupe: new — PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-02 is the hard-cap PARTIAL fabricating scoring_v2 from MISSING_SCORE (different mechanism); PO-RUBRIC-01 is a dimension stamped missing_data while deciding the winner (different direction); M13-11/#PO-region-guard fixed the currency half only. still-open

findings.title: Raw Python exception text is shipped to the client as the user-facing error copy on the text and streaming routes — two production rows read "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'"; the M13-26 fix landed on the camera route only
findings.evidence: structured_comparison_service.py:3659 `return {"success": False, "error": str(e), "total_cost": self.total_cost}` (sync) and :4429 `yield ("error", {"success": False, "error": str(e), ...})` (SSE). text_routes.py:123 `error_msg = result.get("error", "Comparison failed")` and :144 `raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=error_msg)` when no `code` is present — str(e) reaches the wire verbatim. Measured: search_logs carries 2 rows with error_message = "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'" (2026-06-08T22:43:55 and 22:45:22, input_type=text, duration 20,251ms and 19,944ms, products_found=[], cost 0.0). The same string is what _surface_comparison_failure raised to the app. image_routes.py:294 carries the fix and the reason: 'M13-26: never surface str(e) to the client — it embeds hostnames, table names, Postgres codes and upstream URLs' — text_routes has no equivalent.
findings.repro: Read-only SELECT of search_logs (scratchpad/po-rm/sl.py, '== NoneType crashes ==' section). Then read structured_comparison_service.py:3653-3659 and :4424-4431, text_routes.py:121-144, image_routes.py:282-309 at 76ace90.
findings.impact: Two classes of harm from one line. (a) Users: a comparison failure renders a Python AttributeError as the error message — measured twice on the demo query. (b) Disclosure: str(e) on this path can carry Supabase hostnames, table names, Postgres SQLSTATE codes and upstream API URLs, which is exactly why the camera route was fixed; the two highest-traffic routes (/text/compare POST+GET and /text/compare/stream) were left. The SSE variant is worse — the raw string is emitted as the `error` event payload to any connected client.
findings.fix: Apply the M13-26 pattern to structured_comparison_service:3659 and :4429: log str(e) with exc_info at ERROR and Sentry, and return/emit the unified envelope — {success:false, error:<constant copy>, code:'INTERNAL_ERROR', request_id:<request.state.request_id>} — never the exception string. Add a defensive floor in text_routes._surface_comparison_failure:144: when `code` is absent, raise the constant 'Something went wrong on our side.' instead of `error_msg`. Un-flagged (it only narrows what leaves the process). Keep the raw string flowing to log_search's error_message ONLY if that column is treated as internal; it currently is, but a 4096-char exception is also an injection surface into the admin dashboard, so truncate to 200 chars there.
findings.test_first: tests/test_text_route_never_leaks_exception.py: patch the comparison service to return {'success': False, 'error': "relation \"comparisons\" does not exist"} with no 'code', call POST /api/v1/text/compare, assert the 400 body detail does not contain 'relation' and equals the constant copy. RED at HEAD.
findings.dedupe: new — known:M13-26 fixed image_routes only; this is the classic 'fixed-once-never-propagated' theme with two measured production occurrences on the unfixed route. PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-12 covers /text/quick bypassing _surface_comparison_failure, a different route and a different bypass. still-open

findings.title: review_praise — the only review text the app renders — attributes retailer PDP marketing copy to owners verbatim: 8 of 8 recorded strings are "Owners consistently highlight <brand blurb>"
findings.evidence: review_service.py:451 `return f"Owners consistently highlight {woven}."` where woven = `" and ".join(_lower_first(c) for c in positive_clauses)` (:594) and each clause is a highlight `point` with only the "Per <domain>: " prefix removed. The docstring at :518-531 claims the output is 'SYNTHESIZED', 'non-verbatim (never a raw highlight copy)' and 'from real review sentiment'. Measured contradiction, row 2a5d828d p0: review_praise = 'Owners consistently highlight the fragrance opens with a disconcerting burst of effervescent citrus, black truffle, and ylang-ylang and base notes include chocolate, frankincense, patchouli, sandalwood, vanilla, and vetiver' — the identical sentences appear in the same payload's highlights as 'Per myperfumeshop.bh: The fragrance opens with a disconcerting burst...' and 'Per bahrain.sharafdg.com: Base notes include chocolate...'. All 8 recorded review_praise strings are this shape. SmartCompareApp/src/components/results/ResultsAccordion.tsx:363-369 renders review_praise and nothing else from the reviews block.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/misc.txt ('== review_praise strings ==' section) over all 27 rows; cross-referenced against the highlights in audit1.txt. Then read review_service.py:437-455 and :566-600 at 76ace90 (unchanged in shape since the recordings — the lead literal and the join are both still there).
findings.impact: The single most persuasive element on the results screen — social proof — is manufactured. A Tom Ford press release scraped off a retailer PDP is presented to a Bahraini shopper as what OWNERS consistently say. This is a truthfulness failure with regulatory exposure (fabricated consumer testimony), not a copy nit, and it survives every scrub in the pipeline because the scrubs target citation MARKERS and banned VOCABULARY, never the provenance of the sentence. It also defeats the D4 directive it was written to satisfy: removing '[N]' and 'Per <domain>:' made the marketing copy look MORE like a review, not less.
findings.fix: Gate the attribution on provenance, not on cleanliness. Tag each highlight at extraction time with whether its snippet came from a REVIEW surface (a review aggregator, a retailer's reviews endpoint, a forum) or a PDP/marketing surface, and let build_review_praise use only review-sourced clauses; when none survive, return None (the function already contracts to do that and the FE already renders a reviews-empty state, ResultsAccordion.tsx:405). Where only PDP copy exists, either drop the block or re-lead it honestly ('Listings describe it as ...'). Ship behind ENABLE_REVIEW_PRAISE_PROVENANCE_GATE and measure the drop in praise-block coverage — a large drop is the honest number.
findings.test_first: tests/test_review_praise_rejects_pdp_copy.py: feed build_review_praise a reviews dict whose only positive highlight is {'point': 'Per bahrain.sharafdg.com: Quad-camera system with ultra-high-resolution and advanced zoom for professional-grade photography', 'sentiment': 'positive'} and assert the return is None. RED at HEAD (returns 'Owners consistently highlight quad-camera system with...').
findings.dedupe: new — M18's review work and PO-FACTCHECK-CONFIDENCE-08 cover absence-as-verification and the fact_check object; PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-04 covers retailer_quotes never being scrubbed. Nobody has checked what review_praise actually SAYS against where its sentences came from. still-open

findings.title: Every failure-path log_search call omits cost=, so 100% of failed comparisons (3,254 rows, 24.6% of the series) are recorded at $0 despite burning OpenAI and Serper calls for up to 66 seconds
findings.evidence: database_service.py:466-475 declares `cost: float = 0.0, duration_ms: int = 0`. The 8 call sites at HEAD: text_routes.py:268 (POST success) and :417 (GET success) and :638 (stream success) and image_routes.py:255 (camera success) all pass `cost=result.get('metadata', {}).get('total_cost', 0)`; text_routes.py:230 (POST failure), :386 (GET failure), :662 (stream failure) and image_routes.py:285 (camera failure) pass NO cost argument. Measured consequence over 13,237 rows: 'cost>0 rows that FAILED: 0, their cost sum=0.0000' — not one failed row in three months carries a cost. Among the failures are 209 rows that ran to a timeout (one at 66,496ms) and 443 'Comparison data was incomplete' rows, all of which had already paid for the identify + specs + reviews calls.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/sl.py '== COST ==' section over all 13,237 rows; then `grep -rn 'log_search(' app/` at 76ace90 and read each of the 8 sites.
findings.impact: The cost ledger is structurally blind to a quarter of spend, and it is blind exactly where spend is least controlled — a request that ran 30-66 seconds through the full cascade and then failed. analytics_service.get_cost_trends (:80) and get_daily_stats (:28) sum this column, so /admin/costs under-reports, and any MAX_MONTHLY_COST-style guard reading it under-counts in the same direction. On the organic subset the failed 20% of requests are the expensive ones (they ran the full 30s), so the true under-report is worse than 20%.
findings.fix: Thread the cost through the failure paths. The sync/GET handlers already hold `result`, so pass `cost=result.get('metadata', {}).get('total_cost', 0)` at text_routes.py:230 and :386. The streaming failure branch (:662) and the camera failure branch (image_routes.py:285) need the orchestrator's accumulated `self.total_cost` — the sync error return at structured_comparison_service.py:3659 already includes `total_cost`, and the SSE error payload at :4429 does too, so read it from there. Un-flagged; it only adds a number to an existing insert. Then re-baseline the cost KPI, because it will rise.
findings.test_first: tests/test_failure_logs_cost.py: patch the comparison service to return {'success': False, 'error': 'x', 'total_cost': 0.017} and assert the log_search call recorded for the failure carries cost == 0.017. RED at HEAD (0.0).
findings.dedupe: possibly known:#66 (admin cost meters wrong) by title — I could not read the issue body (github MCP failed to connect). If #66 covers the /admin/costs arithmetic, this is a distinct upstream cause: the column itself is never written on failure. still-open

findings.title: The "cost per compare collapsed from $20.53/mo to $0.29/mo" story is a traffic-mix artifact: the measured organic unit cost is $0.0140 per successful compare and has not been re-measured since June
findings.evidence: Raw per-month cost sums are June $20.5276 / July $2.1733 / Aug $0.2890 (matching the campaign baseline). Naive cost-per-success: June $0.00294, July $0.00089, Aug $0.00054. But rows_with_cost is only 3,897/9,157 in June, 1,232/3,363 in July, 289/714 in August — the rest are probe rows logged at 0. On the 1,513-row ORGANIC subset: total cost $17.0013 over 1,210 successes = $0.01405 per successful compare, with 1,207 of 1,513 rows carrying a nonzero cost and only 3 of 1,210 successes at zero. Organic rows by month: June 1,426, July 86, August 1. So the August 'cost' figure is computed over essentially zero real comparisons.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/sl.py '== COST ==' and scratchpad/po-rm/zero.txt 'ORGANIC-LOOKING subset' + the organic-cost block; both over the full 13,237-row pull.
findings.impact: $0.0140 is 4.8x the number the raw series implies and 26x the August figure, and it is the only unit-economics input the project has. Any margin model, free-tier limit or activation gate built on the $0.0003-$0.0005 range is wrong by more than an order of magnitude. Compounded by finding 07 (failures logged at $0), the true organic unit cost is higher still — the 303 organic failures burned real calls and are recorded at zero.
findings.fix: Same probe filter as finding 01, applied to analytics_service.get_cost_trends and get_daily_stats, plus finding 07's cost-on-failure fix; then publish a single measured number: total cost / successful organic compares, per month, with n. Until then, treat $0.0140 as the floor in every economics model and stop quoting the monthly totals as a cost trend — they are a traffic-volume trend.
findings.test_first: tests/test_cost_trends_excludes_probes.py: seed 100 probe rows at cost 0 and 10 organic rows at cost 0.014, assert get_cost_trends()['avg_cost_per_comparison'] == 0.014 not 0.00127. RED at HEAD.
findings.dedupe: new — the June->August cost curve appears in the campaign brief and RUNS.md as evidence of a cost win; nobody split it by traffic type. still-open

findings.title: "We need a moment more on these two — give it another tap" invites a retry that measurably never works: 0 of 228 rows produced a success on any retry, at either a 2-minute or a 10-minute window
findings.evidence: Retry-success computed for every failure string (same normalized query, a later row within the window, any success): 'We need a moment more on these two — give it another tap.' n=228, retried within 2min = 21, within 10min = 98, successes = 0 and 0. 'We don't compare this category' n=690, 271 retried in 2min, 398 in 10min, 0 successes. 'blocked' n=215, 84 retried in 10min, 0 successes. 'Comparison data was incomplete' n=443, 165 retried in 10min, 1 success. Contrast — the copy that IS honest: 'Still gathering prices — give it another tap in a moment.' n=1,288, 893 retried in 2min -> 640 successes (50%), 1,037 in 10min -> 818 (64%); and 'We couldn't finish this comparison in time. Try again.' n=209 -> 28% recovery at 10min.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/sl2.py '== RETRY-SUCCESS ==' section over all 13,237 rows, both windows.
findings.impact: Three of the six user-facing failure strings promise or imply that tapping again will help, and for two of them the measured recovery rate is exactly zero across 3 months. Users burn a rate-limit slot, a usage credit (refunded, but the daily counter round-trips) and 20-30 seconds per pointless retry, and the app teaches them that its error copy is not to be trusted. 271 users retried a category rejection within two minutes — the copy gives them no reason not to.
findings.fix: Split the copy by whether the condition is transient. Keep 'give it another tap' ONLY for the timeout/partial family (measured 50-64% recovery). For the category/content refusal and for the 'incomplete' terminal state, say what the user should do instead ('We can't compare these two — try two products in the same category') and suppress the retry affordance in the client. The strings live in SmartCompareApp/src/i18n/en.json ('home.errors.*') and in structured_comparison_service.py:1389; change both together and add the pair to SmartCompareApp/__tests__/copy-policy.test.ts so a retry-inviting phrase cannot be attached to a terminal code. Un-flagged.
findings.test_first: SmartCompareApp/__tests__/copy-policy.test.ts: assert that no i18n string mapped to a terminal error code (CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE, INSUFFICIENT_DATA) matches /another tap|try again|moment more/i. RED at HEAD.
findings.dedupe: new — PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-11 covers the 'incomplete' string blaming the user, and PO-CATEGORIES-I18N-03 covers a parse failure being normalized to TIMEOUT; neither measures whether the retry the copy invites ever works. still-open

findings.title: The streaming route logs success on any complete payload — including a 30s hard-cap PARTIAL with zero prices — and its third finally branch logs nothing at all, so text_stream shows 721/721 success and zero failures lifetime
findings.evidence: text_routes.py:593-601 sets complete_response on 'complete' or 'settle_complete' and had_error only on an 'error' event; :630 `if complete_response and not had_error and not complete_after_client_gone:` logs success=True; :659 logs the constant 'Streaming comparison failed'; :676 the `else` branch (mid-stream raise, cancel, GeneratorExit, payload-after-disconnect) refunds a credit and logs NOTHING. Measured: 721 text_stream rows since 2026-06-01 (1,162 lifetime), ALL success=True; zero rows carry 'Streaming comparison failed' anywhere in the table. 711 of the 721 have an EMPTY products_found array and only 10 carry a nonzero cost. The recorded comparisons corroborate that a hard-cap partial reaches 'complete': rows 779200c0 and 9a24786f carry metadata.partial=True at elapsed_seconds 30.0 with both prices unavailable, and both were persisted as normal comparisons.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/sl.py '== PER input_type ==' and sl2.py '== text_stream duration distribution ==' over the full pull; lifetime input_type counts via count='exact'. Then read text_routes.py:586-690 at 76ace90.
findings.impact: The path the shipped app actually uses has no failure telemetry. 'text_stream 100% success' is a definition, not an outcome: a 30-second timeout that ships a partial with no prices is a success row, and a mid-stream crash is no row at all. Every success-rate, cost and latency number for the streaming route is therefore uninformative, and #64 (SSE analytics/quota keyed on the success flag) sits on top of the same flag. It also means the 25% failure rate everyone quotes is a TEXT-route number that says nothing about the route users are on.
findings.fix: Three changes in the finally block. (1) Log the partial honestly: read complete_response['metadata'].get('partial') and log success=False with error_message='partial_hard_cap' (or a `partial` boolean column) rather than success=True. (2) Give the `else` branch at :676 its own log_search with an error_message that distinguishes client_disconnect from mid_stream_error — right now the most interesting failures are the invisible ones. (3) Carry the orchestrator's total_cost into both failure logs (finding 07). Un-flagged; it changes only what is written to search_logs. Then re-measure the streaming success rate before anyone quotes it.

findings.title: 42.8% of the price cache (1,689 of 3,945 rows) is a GPT training-data guess, and 151 rows carry `gpt_organic_extract`, a source_method in neither the showable set nor any eval provenance bucket
findings.evidence: product_prices source_method totals over all 3,945 rows: estimated 1,689 (42.8%, every one with url=NULL), local_bhd 1,484, page_scrape_jsonld 268, woo_store_api 222, gpt_organic_extract 151, converted_usd 79, zyte_render_bhd 27, magento_graphql_bhd 11, shopify_json 10, scrapedo_rendered 4. `_showable_source_methods()` (price_service.py:1623) = `_GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS | {'converted_usd'}` — it contains neither `estimated` nor `gpt_organic_extract`. eval_runner.py:431-455 partitions produced prices into genuine_bh / converted_usd / estimated and documents that 'an unrecognized non-empty method counts toward priced but no bucket' — `gpt_organic_extract` is exactly that case, so 151 cached prices inflate the `priced` denominator while landing in no bucket, silently depressing every provenance share.
findings.repro: Read-only SELECT * FROM product_prices (3,945 rows), scratchpad/po-rm/pp.py -> pp.txt; then read price_service.py:1620-1625 and eval_runner.py:431-460 at 76ace90.
findings.impact: Nearly half the cache is unshowable by construction, so a cache hit on those rows guarantees a price-pending card after paying the lookup — the cache is storing the answer 'we don't know'. The 151 unbucketed rows are the failure mode eval_runner's own comment warns about: the genuine-BH-share denominator counts them, the numerator cannot, so the KPI reads low for a reason nobody can see in the dashboard. Together with finding 02 (the numerator is 82% mislabelled), the provenance KPI is wrong in both directions at once.
findings.fix: Two separate things. (a) Stop caching `estimated`: a Tier-3 GPT guess has no shelf life and cannot be shown, so should_cache_price must reject it — that reclaims 43% of the cache and removes a class of useless hits. (b) Either add `gpt_organic_extract` to the eval partition explicitly (as its own bucket, not as genuine) and to a documented non-showable list, or rename it to `estimated` if that is what it is; then extend tests/test_eval_genuine_methods_parity.py from 'the two GENUINE sets are equal' to 'every method any writer emits appears in exactly one eval bucket'. Un-flagged.
findings.test_first: tests/test_source_method_partition_total.py: enumerate every string literal assigned to 'source_method' across app/services/*.py and assert each appears in exactly one of GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS / {'converted_usd'} / {'estimated'} / an explicit NON_SHOWABLE set. findings.title: On organic traffic 15.4% of comparisons terminate at the 30s hard cap and 2.6% exceed it; measured stage timings show the verdict LLM call alone consumes 3.8-11.0s and per-product price fetch 6.5-15.9s
findings.evidence: Organic subset (n=1,513) duration histogram: 15-25s 764 (50.5%), 25-29.5s 255 (16.9%), 29.5-31.5s = the 30s cap 233 (15.4%), <5s 114, 5-15s 105, >31.5s 40 (2.6%), 0ms 2. Success-only p50=21,954ms p90=29,540 p95=30,004 p99=30,637. metadata.stage_timings_ms on the 7 rows that carry it: verdict_ms = 10,991.8 / 10,475.9 / 7,004.0 / 5,767.9 / 4,802.0 / 4,453.4 / 3,816.3; scoring_ms = 0.2-5.0 (negligible); response_build_ms = 0.3-3.4; per-product price_ms up to 15,917.1 and 15,237.3 in the same request; image_url_ms 345.8-4,377.4; unaccounted wall (total minus verdict+scoring+build minus max(phase1+phase2)) = 527.8 to 5,204.2ms. In row 1c442680 verdict_ms 10,475.9 of total 14,989.1 = 69.9% of the request.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/zero.txt (organic buckets) and stage.txt (per-row stage decomposition over the 7 rows carrying stage_timings_ms), both from the read-only pulls. STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 confirmed in baseline/railway-web-vars.txt.
findings.impact: Nearly one in six real comparisons is cut off by the cap rather than finishing, and those users get the partial shape — which finding 04 shows still declares a winner and finding 10 shows is logged as a success. The two levers are visible and unequal: the verdict call is a single serial LLM request costing up to 11s (70% of a fast request), and price fetch costs up to 16s per product. Scoring and response building are free (sub-5ms). Any latency work that does not attack verdict_ms and price_ms is attacking 3% of the budget.
findings.fix: Attack the two measured stages, in order. (a) verdict_ms: it runs at priority='high' on gpt-4o (structured_comparison_service.py:777 per the sibling lane); cap its max_tokens, stream it, or start it against the scored dimensions the moment scoring completes (scoring_ms is 0.3ms, so nothing is waiting on it) rather than after the full gather. (b) price_ms: the fan-out is already parallel per product but 15.9s says a tier is running to its own timeout — bound the per-tier deadline so the pair budget is < 12s, and drop the tiers whose output the chokepoint pends anyway (finding 03). (c) Emit stage_timings_ms on every response, not just when DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS is set — n=7 is not a latency dataset. All three are flag-gatable; (c) ships first because the others cannot be measured without it.
findings.test_first: tests/test_stage_timings_always_emitted.py: run the sync compare path with DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS unset and assert result['metadata']['stage_timings_ms']['verdict_ms'] is a float. RED at HEAD (key absent).
findings.dedupe: new — M18's load answer is explicitly MODELLED ('all concurrency numbers MODELLED'); this is the first measured per-stage decomposition and the first cap-hit rate computed on organic traffic. Complements rather than repeats the load lane. still-open

findings.title: overview.winner.name names the OTHER product than overview.winner.product_index in 2 recorded rows, and comparison.winner_index disagrees with the other three index fields in exactly those rows
findings.evidence: Rows 11651c1d and f79c5403 (2026-05-28, 12 seconds apart, same query): products = ['Manama Pickles Achbara Sauce', 'Manama Pickles Maabooch Kuwaiti Red 250g']; overview.winner.product_index = 0, scoring_v2.overall_score.winner_idx = 0, top-level winner_index = 0, but overview.winner.name = 'Manama Pickles Maabooch Kuwaiti Red 250g' (products[1]) and comparison.winner_index = 1. eval_runner.extract_winner_index (which reads scoring_v2 first, by dispatcher rule) returns 0 for both. The same payloads carry scoring_v2.overall_score product_a=74 product_b=74, win_margin=0, and factual_verdict.line1 = 'Manama Pickles Achbara Sauce comes in 0% cheaper.' — so the payload simultaneously says the two are tied, that product 0 wins, that product 1 is the winner by name, and that product 0 is 0% cheaper. Index-agreement check over all 27 rows: 2 rows disagree, 25 agree.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/quant.py '== WINNER INDEX MISMATCH ==' and '== WINNER NAME != products[index].name ==' over all 27 rows (5 index fields each). audit1.txt carries the full payload extract for both rows.
findings.impact: On an exact score tie the payload contains two different answers to the only question the product exists to answer, and which one the user sees depends on whether the client renders by index (the winner card, the highlighted column) or by name (the declaration string). Both recorded occurrences are ties (win_margin 0), which is the regime the tie-break was supposed to make deterministic — so the disagreement is systematic at parity, not random. 2 of 23 rows with a winner block is 8.7%.
findings.fix: Make the name a derivation, never an independent value: build overview.winner.name as products[winner_index]['name'] at the single projection site rather than accepting whatever the verdict model returned, and drop comparison.winner_index in favour of the deterministic index (or assert them equal and log GPT_WINNER_DISAGREES, which response_builder.py:1398 already does for the independent-winner case but does not do for this field). Pair it with the tie-break: PO-RUBRIC-05 reports the coverage tie-break is behind a dark flag, so at parity the order is caller-dependent — fixing the name without fixing the tie-break just makes the coin-flip consistent. Un-flagged.
findings.test_first: tests/test_winner_name_follows_index.py: build a response where the GPT comparison dict returns winner_index=1 while scoring_result picks 0, and assert overview.winner.name == products[0]['name'] and comparison.winner_index == 0. RED at HEAD.
findings.dedupe: new — PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-06 covers an exact tie asserting both 'equal' and 'A beats B by 1' inside scoring_v2/overview numbers; PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-10 covers an out-of-range winner_index raising IndexError. Neither covers winner.name pointing at the other product, and neither has the recorded occurrences. still-open

findings.title: clean_review_citations converts a [N] marker into a literal "Per <domain>: " prefix instead of removing it — 146 of 188 recorded review bullets (78%) ship a raw citation artifact into the persisted payload
findings.evidence: review_service.py:157-159 `def _attribute(num): domain = snippet_source_map.get(num, ''); return f"Per {domain}: " if domain else ""`, applied by replace_citation to review_summary.highlights[].point (:195) and retailer_quotes[].text (:203). Measured over the 188 highlight bullets in the 27 recorded payloads: 71 still start with a bare '[N]' (the snippet_source_map missed the index, so the marker is left verbatim), 46 start with '[<host>]' (e.g. '[rtings.com]', '[techpowerup.com]'), 29 start with 'Per <host>: ' (the cleaner's own output), and only 42 (22.3%) are clean. Three different citation formats appear inside the same product's bullet list (row eaf479bb).
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/quant.py '== CITATION MARKER LEAK IN HIGHLIGHTS ==' over all 27 rows; examples in quant.txt. Then read review_service.py:145-210 at 76ace90.
findings.impact: Bounded because SmartCompareApp/src/components/results/ResultsAccordion.tsx:363-369 renders review_praise and never highlights, so at HEAD these strings are not on screen — but they ARE persisted into comparisons.full_response, shipped over the wire on every compare and share, and returned by the history and share endpoints, so any future consumer (and any partner reading the API) gets them. More importantly they are the INPUT to build_review_praise: the de-attribution at review_service.py:353-362 exists only because this function inserted the attribution in the first place, and finding 06 shows what survives that round trip.
findings.fix: Remove citation markers rather than rewriting them into prose. Keep the resolved domain as structured data — `highlights[].source_domain` — and strip the marker from `point` entirely; then build_review_praise can gate on source_domain (finding 06's fix) instead of pattern-matching a prefix it inserted, and the _PER_DOMAIN_PREFIX_RE / 'Per :' / 'Per bn.:' salvage code at :330-365 can be deleted. Also fix the 71 unmapped '[N]' cases: when snippet_source_map has no entry, strip the marker instead of leaving it. Un-flagged (no user-visible surface changes at HEAD); it makes finding 06's fix implementable.
findings.test_first: tests/test_clean_review_citations_strips.py: feed clean_review_citations a highlight '[6] Great battery' with a snippet_source_map hit for '6' and assert the result point == 'Great battery' and point does not contain 'Per '. RED at HEAD ('Per rtings.com: Great battery').
findings.dedupe: new — M5/Task C5 are the changes that CREATED this shape and are cited in the code; no review has measured what fraction of shipped bullets carry a marker or noticed that the cleaner's output is itself an artifact. still-open

findings.title: 84% of price URLs ever shipped point at a search results page, not a product page — the buy link lands the user somewhere the quoted price does not appear
findings.evidence: Classification of all 52 recorded product price cells: no_url 16, google_shopping_search 15, site_search 10, pdp_like 5, no_price 6. Of the 31 cells that shipped both an amount and a URL, 26 (83.9%) are a search page: 15 `https://www.google.com/search?ibp=oshop&q=...`, and 10 site searches (`uae.sharafdg.com/search/?q=`, `www.extra.com/en-sa/search/?q=`, `www.noon.com/search?q=`, `bh.iherb.com/search?kw=`). Only 5 are a PDP (4 tomford.com, 1 bh.iherb.com/pr/). At HEAD the two producers are unchanged: price_service.py:9678 takes Serper's `link` verbatim, and the RETAILER_SEARCH_URLS table at :260-275 is entirely search templates — amazon `/s?k=`, walmart `/search?q=`, best buy `searchpage.jsp?st=`, target `/s?searchTerm=`, costco `CatalogSearch`, newegg `/p/pl?d=`, noon `/search?q=`, jarir `catalogsearch`.
findings.repro: scratchpad/po-rm/quant.py '== URL KINDS ==' and '== retailer hosts on price.url ==' over all 27 payloads; then read price_service.py:255-300 and :9670-9690 at 76ace90.
findings.impact: The price is the product's core claim and its evidence link does not resolve to the evidence. A user checking '259.44 BHD at Best Buy' lands on a Google Shopping search whose results, currency and prices differ from the card. It also removes the only affordance that could turn a comparison into a purchase (the affiliate path this business depends on). Note the interaction with finding 03: the same URLs that mislead the user are the ones HEAD's chokepoint now pends, so the choice today is a misleading link or no price — fixing the URL fixes both.
findings.fix: Same as finding 03's option (a), plus a table cleanup: RETAILER_SEARCH_URLS should not be a fallback for a SHOWN price at all. Resolve to a PDP before selection (select_best already takes require_url=True and rejects non-PDP URLs — route the shopping tier through it instead of its own inline sort at :9707-9745), and where no PDP resolves, ship the price with no url rather than a search link. Keep the search templates only for the discovery/diagnostic surface. Behind the same ENABLE_SHOPPING_DISCOVERY_URL_SPLIT flag as finding 03.
findings.test_first: tests/test_shown_price_url_is_pdp.py: for every recorded fixture payload in tests/fixtures/comparison_baseline_d2*.json, assert that any overview.products[i].price.url is not is_non_pdp_listing_url(). RED at HEAD.

The wrong-COUNTRY half of these URLs (uae.sharafdg / extra /en-sa) was fixed post-recording by L1.3 (price_service.py:276-290) — that half is a status line, the search-page half is live. still-open

findings.title: Only 37 of 16,283 search_logs rows (0.23%) carry a user_id, so every per-user, cohort and retention analytic has at most 37 lifetime observations
findings.evidence: `SELECT count(*) FROM search_logs WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL` = 37 against a 16,283-row table. database_service.py:499-500 `if user_id: record["user_id"] = user_id` — the column is only written when the caller supplies one, and the caller supplies `user.get('id') if user else None`, so every anonymous request (which is essentially all of them, including all 13 probe queries) writes NULL. Corroborating: all 27 rows in `comparisons` DO carry a user_id, so authenticated comparisons happened; their search_logs siblings are among the 37.
findings.repro: count='exact' with .not_.is_('user_id','null') against search_logs (scratchpad/po-rm/pull2.py -> pull2.txt).
findings.impact: Nothing user-shaped can be measured from the outcome table: no per-user success rate, no repeat-use curve, no cohort effect, no free-tier consumption pattern, no abuse signal keyed to an account. Combined with finding 01 (88.6% probe traffic), the product has 37 lifetime rows that describe a real signed-in person's experience. Any activation decision framed as 'users are doing X' has no data behind it, and #65 (behavior profile reads phantom columns, personalization DEAD) means the other per-user substrate is dead too — so the personalization the payloads advertise (scoring_method='personalized' on 26 recorded rows) is built on nothing measurable.
findings.fix: Write a stable anonymous identifier alongside user_id — the device fingerprint the anon usage gate already computes (usage_service.valid_device_fingerprint) or a hashed request-scoped anon id — into a new `anon_id` column, so sessions can be counted without identifying anyone; keep user_id as-is. Then the outcome table can answer repeat-use questions for the 99.8% of traffic that is anonymous. Ships with the migration; note migrations 033/034/035/036 are already written and UNAPPLIED, so this one must not be stacked behind them silently. Independently, treat 'we have 37 authenticated observations' as the honest headline in any KPI review.
findings.test_first: tests/test_log_search_records_anon_id.py: call log_search with user_id=None and device_fingerprint='abc' and assert the inserted record carries a non-null anon identifier. RED at HEAD (no such field).
findings.dedupe: new — #65 covers the behavior-profile phantom columns (personalization dead); this is the outcome table having no subject at all. Not previously measured. still-open

findings.title: P3 sweep: seven smaller recorded/measured defects found while checking every cell
findings.evidence: (a) SOURCE-LESS STAR RATINGS, fixed-at-HEAD: 17 of 46 recorded review cells shipped a rating (3.5/3.6/3.7/3.8/4.0/4.3/4.5) with rating_source=None and review_count=None; the source is response_builder.py:1417-1421 `pd_item['rating'] = derive_rating_from_scores(overall)` — a rating derived FROM the score. HEAD sets rating_derived=True there and both projections null it (:1703, :1774), so the leak is closed; the circularity (a star rating manufactured from the score it will later appear to corroborate) is not. (b) L2 MODERATION REFUSES A MAINSTREAM FRAGRANCE: 2 of the 690 'We don't compare this category' rows are 'YSL Black Opium vs Lancome La Vie Est Belle'. HEAD's L1 blocklist is clean — content_blocklist.json lists 'opium tincture'/'opium poppy'/'raw opium', not 'opium', and ContentSafetyService.check_query_intent returns allowed=True for that query and for 14 other GCC probes (Dior Poison, Kush hair oil, Hemp shampoo, Marlboro/Camel, Absolut, Bacardi rum cake, Panadol, Lattafa) — so the refusal came from the L2 GPT moderation pass, which has no allowlist for cosmetics naming. (c) SUPPLEMENT UNIT-PRICE FALLACY, fixed-at-HEAD: row 894d1926 declares 'HealthAid Vitamin D3 1000 IU is 53% cheaper at 2.07 BHD for 120 tablets compared to NOW's 4.388 BHD for 360 softgels' — 0.01725 vs 0.01219 per unit, i.e. the 'cheaper' winner is 41.5% MORE expensive per unit. reconcile_pair_fairness (price_service.py:3024, called unconditionally at structured_comparison_service.py:3373) now targets a common unit count for supplements and pends the side that cannot reach it. (d) TWO CACHED COMPARISONS OF THE SAME QUERY, OPPOSITE WINNERS: rows eaf479bb and 4b4ad16a ('iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24', 88 seconds apart, both cached=False) crown Galaxy S24 and then iPhone 15, because the Galaxy price moved 350.0 -> 399.0 BHD between two different retailers; both prices stamped local_bhd and both confidence.price.method='retailer_verified'/'live'. (e) ENABLE_REGION_CURRENCY_GUARD IS DARK IN PROD: it is absent from the Railway `web` variable list and defaults OFF (price_service.py:686), so the only guard that would pend a currency-mismatched price never runs — the mitigation for the M13-11 hazard is off in the environment that ships. (f) BRAND DOUBLING IN THE DECLARATION: row 779200c0 renders overview.winner.name = 'TOM FORD TOM FORD SOLEIL NEIGE 100ML' and 12 of the 27 rows carry a doubled brand in product_names ('Apple Apple iPhone 14', 'Louis Vuitton Louis Vuitton LV Vers Mesh Cap', 'HealthAid HealthAid Vitamin D3'); 5 further rows have winner.name brand-prefixed where the card label is not ('Samsung Galaxy S24' vs 'Galaxy S24') — dedupe known:PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-07, still-open, now with counts. (g) _lower_first MANGLES PROPER NOUNS IN THE ONE RENDERED REVIEW STRING: review_service.py:594 lowercases the first character of each clause, producing 'Owners consistently highlight oud Voyager redefines oud with luminous floral depth' in 3 recorded payloads.
findings.repro: All from the same read-only pulls: scratchpad/po-rm/quant.py (a, d, f), t_safety2.py + app/data/content_blocklist.json (b), misc.txt (c, g), baseline/railway-web-vars.txt + price_service.py:686 (e). Line numbers read from the materialized 76ace90 tree.
findings.impact: Individually small. (a) and (c) are closed and are reported as status so nobody re-finds them. (b) costs a handful of legitimate fragrance comparisons and, at the measured volume, is not worth a code change before the L2 pass is instrumented. (d) is the honest face of finding 02 — provenance labelled 'live retailer verified' that changes the winner between two runs 88 seconds apart. (e) is the one to act on: a dark guard is not a guard, and it is the second half of the M13-11 fix. (f) and (g) are copy defects on the two most-read strings in the product.
findings.fix: Act on (e) first: turn ENABLE_REGION_CURRENCY_GUARD on in the Railway `web` service and measure the pend-rate delta, since the pre-scoring half already exists and is a no-op today. For (b), log the L2 refusal reason to search_logs so the over-rejection rate is measurable before anyone tunes the prompt. For (g), lowercase only when the clause's first token is not capitalised mid-sentence elsewhere in the source, or drop _lower_first and choose the glue by clause shape (the code already does this for the lead). For (a)'s residual circularity, stop deriving a rating from the score at all — a null rating is honest and the FE already handles it (ResultsAccordion.tsx:388 skips a product with no review signal). (d) and (f) are covered by findings 02/14 and PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-07.
findings.test_first: One per item; the load-bearing one is (e): tests/test_region_currency_guard_prod_default.py asserting that with ENABLE_REGION_CURRENCY_GUARD unset, apply_region_currency_guard returns False and changes nothing — which is GREEN at HEAD and documents that prod runs without the guard, so flipping it is a deliberate, tested change rather than a surprise.
findings.dedupe: (a) recorded-then, FIXED-at-HEAD — status only. (c) recorded-then, FIXED-at-HEAD — status only. (f) known:PO-VERDICT-TRUTH-07 still-open with fresh counts. (b), (d), (e), (g) new.
